translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 291
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 291

sentences.zh: 【後周紀二】　起玄黓困敦九月，盡閼逢攝提格四月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Zhou Records 2] From the ninth month of Xuanqu Kundun through the fourth month of Yanfeng Shetige; a little more than one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Zhou Records 2] From the ninth month of Xuanqu Kundun through the fourth month of Yanfeng Shetige—a span of somewhat more than one year.

sentences.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武皇帝中廣順二年（

translations.literal: Mid-annals of Taizu the Sagely Divine, Respectful, Solemn, and Martial Cultural Emperor—Guangshun year two (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Central Annals of Emperor Taizu of Later Zhou, Guangshun year two (

sentences.zh: 壬子，公元九五二年）

translations.literal: Renzi, equivalent to the year 952 CE)
translations.idiomatic: 952 CE, year renzi of the cycle)

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅朔，吳越丞相裴堅卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day of the jiayin new moon, Pei Jian, Chancellor of Wuyue, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiayin, the first day of the month, Pei Jian, chancellor of Wuyue, died.

sentences.zh: 以台州刺史吳延福同參相府事。

translations.literal: Wu Yanfu, Prefect of Taizhou, was appointed to participate jointly in the affairs of the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yanfu, prefect of Taizhou, was named to assist in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 庚午，敕北邊吏民毋得入契丹境俘掠。

translations.literal: On gengwu, an edict commanded that officials and commoners on the northern frontier must not enter Khitan territory to raid and carry off captives.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, an edict forbade frontier officials and civilians to cross into Khitan lands to raid and seize prisoners.

sentences.zh: 契丹將高謨翰以葦筏渡胡盧河入寇，至冀州，成德節度使何福進遣龍捷都指揮使劉誠誨等屯貝州以拒之。

translations.literal: The Khitan general Gao Mohan crossed the Hulu River on reed rafts to invade, reaching Jizhou. He Fuqin, Military Governor of Chengde, sent Liu Chenghui, Commander of the Longjie Army, and others to encamp at Beizhou to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan general Gao Mohan rafted across the Hulu River on reed floats and raided as far as Jizhou. He Fuqin, military governor of Chengde, sent Longjie army commander Liu Chenghui and others to hold Beizhou against him.

sentences.zh: 契丹聞之，遽引兵北渡。

translations.literal: When the Khitan heard of this, they hastily withdrew their troops north across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the Khitan promptly pulled their army back north across the river.

sentences.zh: 所掠冀州丁壯數百人，望見官軍，爭鼓噪，欲攻契丹，官軍不敢應，契丹盡殺之。

translations.literal: Several hundred able-bodied men of Jizhou whom they had seized, seeing the government troops, clamored to attack the Khitan, but the government troops dared not respond, and the Khitan killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred able-bodied men from Jizhou whom they had taken captive, sighting the imperial army, raised a clamor and tried to turn on the Khitan; the government forces did not dare answer them, and the Khitan slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 蜀山南西道節度使李廷珪奏周人聚兵關中，請益兵為備。

translations.literal: Li Tinggui, Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit in Shu, memorialized that the Zhou were massing troops in Guanzhong and requested reinforcements as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tinggui, Shu military governor of Shannan West Circuit, reported that the Zhou were concentrating forces in Guanzhong and asked for more troops to guard against them.

sentences.zh: 蜀主遣奉鑾肅衛都虞候趙進將兵趣利州，既而聞周人聚兵以備北漢，乃引還。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler sent Zhao Jin, Deputy Commander of the Fengluan and Suwei Guards, to lead troops toward Lizhou; later, hearing that the Zhou were massing troops against Northern Han, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler sent Zhao Jin, deputy commander of the palace guard, to march on Lizhou; when he learned the Zhou buildup was aimed at Northern Han, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 唐武安節度使邊鎬，昏懦無斷，在湖南，政出多門，不合眾心。

translations.literal: Bian Hao, Military Governor of Wu'an in Tang, was muddle-headed, timid, and indecisive. In Hunan, government issued from many hands and did not accord with popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao, Tang military governor of Wu'an, was dull-witted, timid, and unable to decide. In Hunan, authority was scattered among many hands and failed to win the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 吉水人歐陽廣上書，言：「鎬非將帥才，必喪湖南，宜別擇良帥，益兵以救其敗。」

translations.literal: Ouyang Guang of Jishui submitted a memorial, saying: "Bian Hao is not a general's material; he is sure to lose Hunan. Another able commander should be chosen and more troops sent to avert defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Guang of Jishui submitted a memorial stating: "Bian Hao lacks the talent of a commander-in-chief and will surely lose Hunan. You should select another capable general and reinforce the army before disaster strikes."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No answer was returned.

sentences.zh: 唐主使鎬經略朗州，有自朗州來者，多言劉言忠順，鎬由是不為備。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler had Bian Hao oversee Langzhou. Visitors from Langzhou repeatedly said that Liu Yan was loyal and obedient, and on this account Bian Hao made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent Bian Hao to manage affairs at Langzhou. Travelers from Langzhou kept reporting that Liu Yan was loyal, and Bian Hao therefore took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 唐主召劉言入朝，言不行，謂王逵曰：「唐必伐我，奈何？」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler summoned Liu Yan to court, but Yan would not go. He said to Wang Kui: "Tang is sure to attack us. What are we to do?"
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler summoned Liu Yan to court, but Yan refused to go. He said to Wang Kui, "Tang will certainly attack us—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「武陵負江湖之險，帶甲數萬，安能拱手受制於人！

translations.literal: Kui replied: "Wuling rests on the defenses of rivers and lakes and fields tens of thousands of armored men. How could we meekly submit to another's control!
translations.idiomatic: Kui replied, "Wuling holds the natural defenses of river and lake country and tens of thousands of armed men—how could we simply hand ourselves over to someone else!

sentences.zh: 邊鎬撫馭無方，士民不附，可一戰擒也。」

translations.literal: Bian Hao governs without method; soldiers and civilians do not attach themselves to him. He can be seized in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao has no skill in winning men over; troops and people alike do not stand with him. We can take him in one fight."

sentences.zh: 言猶豫未決，周行逢曰：「機事貴速，緩則彼為之備，不可圖也。」

translations.literal: Yan hesitated and could not decide. Zhou Xingfeng said: "Opportunity favors speed; if we delay, the enemy will prepare, and the plan cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Yan still wavered. Zhou Xingfeng said, "Opportunities demand speed—if we wait, they will ready their defenses and the chance will be lost."

sentences.zh: 言乃以逵、行逢及牙將何敬真、張仿、蒲公益、朱全琇、宇文瓊、彭萬和、潘叔嗣、張文表十人皆為指揮使，部分發兵。

translations.literal: Yan then appointed Kui, Xingfeng, and the staff generals He Jingzhen, Zhang Fang, Pu Gongyi, Zhu Quanxiu, Yuwen Qiong, Peng Wanhe, Pan Shusi, and Zhang Wenbiao—ten men in all—as commanders, and divided the forces to march out.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then named Kui, Xingfeng, and eight staff generals—He Jingzhen, Zhang Fang, Pu Gongyi, Zhu Quanxiu, Yuwen Qiong, Peng Wanhe, Pan Shusi, and Zhang Wenbiao—all commanders, and divided the army for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣、文表，皆朗州人也。

translations.literal: Shusi and Wenbiao were both natives of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shusi and Wenbiao were both men of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 行逢能謀，文表善戰，叔嗣果敢，三人多相須成功，情款甚暱。

translations.literal: Xingfeng was skilled in planning, Wenbiao excelled in battle, and Shusi was bold and resolute. The three often relied on one another for success and were on terms of great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng was a strategist, Wenbiao a fighter, and Shusi bold and decisive; the three often needed one another to win and were bound by deep friendship.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲召漵州酋長苻彥通為援，行逢曰：「蠻貪而無義，前年從馬希萼入潭州，焚掠無遺。

translations.literal: The generals wished to summon Fu Yantong, chieftain of Xuzhou, as an ally. Xingfeng said: "The barbarians are greedy and faithless. Two years ago they followed Ma Xie into Tanzhou and burned and plundered without leaving anything.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to call in Fu Yantong, chieftain of Xuzhou, as reinforcements. Xingfeng said, "The tribes are greedy and treacherous—two years ago they followed Ma Xie into Tanzhou and left nothing unburned or unplundered.

sentences.zh: 吾兵以義舉，往無不克，烏用此物，使暴殄百姓哉！」

translations.literal: Our army acts on righteous grounds and has never failed to prevail—why use such creatures and let them ravage the people!"
translations.idiomatic: Our forces fight in a just cause and have never failed—why bring in such allies only to let them slaughter the people!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 然亦畏彥通為後患，以蠻酋土團都指揮使劉□為群蠻所憚，補西境鎮遏使以備之。

translations.literal: Yet they also feared Yantong as a future threat. Because the Man chieftain and local militia commander Liu [character missing in text] was feared by the various tribes, he was appointed Western Border Pacification Commissioner as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Still fearing Yantong as a future menace, they appointed Liu [—], a tribal militia commander whom the various Man groups dreaded, as Western Border Pacification Commissioner to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，逵等將兵分道趣長少，以孫朗、曹進為先鋒使，邊鎬遣指揮使郭再誠等將兵屯益陽以拒之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Kui and the others led troops by separate routes toward Changsha. Sun Lang and Cao Jin were made vanguard commanders. Bian Hao sent the commander Guo Zaicheng and others to encamp at Yiyang to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Kui marched on Changsha by several routes with Sun Lang and Cao Jin as vanguard commanders. Bian Hao sent Guo Zaicheng and other commanders to hold Yiyang against them.

sentences.zh: 戊子，逵等克沅江，執都監劉承遇，裨將李師德帥眾五百降之。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Kui and the others captured Yuanjiang and seized the superintendent Liu Chengyu. The lieutenant Li Shide led five hundred men in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi they took Yuanjiang and captured superintendent Liu Chengyu; lieutenant Li Shide surrendered with five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，逵等命軍士舉小舟自蔽，直造益陽，四面斧寨而入，遂克之，殺戍兵二千人。

translations.literal: On renchen, Kui and the others ordered the soldiers to raise small boats as cover, sailed straight to Yiyang, broke through the stockades on all four sides with axes, and took the place, killing two thousand garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen they had troops hoist small boats for cover, rowed straight to Yiyang, hacked through the palisades on every side, and seized the town, killing two thousand defenders.

sentences.zh: 邊鎬告急於唐。

translations.literal: Bian Hao reported the emergency to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao sent urgent word to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 甲午，逵等克橋口及湘陰，乙未，至潭州。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Kui and the others captured Qiaokou and Xiangyin. On yiwei they reached Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu they took Qiaokou and Xiangyin; on yiwei they arrived at Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 邊鎬嬰城自守，救兵未至，城中兵少。

translations.literal: Bian Hao shut himself in the city to defend it. Relief had not arrived, and troops in the city were few.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hao barricaded himself in the city; reinforcements had not come, and his garrison was weak.

sentences.zh: 丙申夜，鎬棄城走，吏民俱潰。

translations.literal: On the night of bingshen, Hao abandoned the city and fled; officials and people alike broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingshen, Hao fled the city and officials and civilians alike collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 醴陵門橋折，死者萬餘人，道州刺史廖偃為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: The gate bridge at Liling collapsed, and more than ten thousand died. Liao Yan, Prefect of Daozhou, was killed by the disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge at Liling gate gave way and more than ten thousand perished; Liao Yan, prefect of Daozhou, was killed by the fleeing mob.

sentences.zh: 丁酉旦，王逵入城，自稱武平節度副使、權知軍府事，以何敬真為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At dawn on dingyou, Wang Kui entered the city, styled himself Deputy Military Governor of Wuping and provisional administrator of the military government, and appointed He Jingzhen campaigning marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on dingyou, Wang Kui entered the city, proclaimed himself deputy military governor of Wuping and acting head of the military government, and named He Jingzhen campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 遣敬真等追鎬，不及，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: He sent Jingzhen and others in pursuit of Hao but did not overtake him; they beheaded five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jingzhen in pursuit of Hao but failed to catch him, though they took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 薄公益攻岳州，唐岳州刺史宋德權走，劉言以公益權知岳州。

translations.literal: Pu Gongyi attacked Yuezhou. Song Dequan, Tang Prefect of Yuezhou, fled. Liu Yan appointed Gongyi provisional administrator of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Gongyi attacked Yuezhou; Song Dequan, the Tang prefect, fled, and Liu Yan put Gongyi in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐將守湖南諸州者，聞長沙陷，相繼遁去。

translations.literal: Tang generals holding the various prefectures of Hunan, hearing that Changsha had fallen, fled one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Tang commanders holding Hunan's prefectures, learning that Changsha had fallen, abandoned their posts in succession.

sentences.zh: 劉言盡復馬氏嶺北故地，惟郴、連入於南漢。

translations.literal: Liu Yan fully recovered the former Ma domains north of the Ling range; only Chen and Lian fell to Southern Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan restored all the old Ma territory north of the Nanling passes; only Chen and Lian passed to Southern Han.

sentences.zh: 契丹瀛、莫、幽州大水，流民入塞散居河北者數十萬口，契丹州縣亦不之禁。

translations.literal: Great floods struck Ying, Mo, and You prefectures in Khitan territory. Refugees who entered the frontier and scattered through Hebei numbered several hundred thousand mouths, and Khitan prefectures and counties did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Floods devastated Ying, Mo, and You in Khitan lands; refugees who crossed the border and spread through Hebei numbered in the hundreds of thousands, and Khitan local authorities did not stop them.

sentences.zh: 詔所在賑給存處之，中國民先為所掠，得歸者什五六。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that wherever they were, relief be given and they be settled. Of Chinese subjects earlier seized by the Khitan, five or six in ten who could return did so.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered local authorities to provide relief and settle them; of Chinese previously carried off by the Khitan, only about half to three-fifths made it home.

sentences.zh: 丁未，谷以病臂久未癒，三表辭位，帝遣中使諭指曰：「卿所掌至重，朕難其人，苟事功克集，何必朝禮！

translations.literal: On dingwei, Gu Wei, his diseased arm long unhealed, thrice memorialized to resign his post. The emperor sent a palace envoy to convey his intent: "What you oversee is of the utmost weight, and I find no one to replace you. If the work is accomplished, what need is there for court ceremony!
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Gu Wei—his arm ailment still unhealed after a long while—submitted three memorials resigning office. The emperor sent a palace envoy with this message: "Your charge is too vital for me to replace you; if the tasks are done, why insist on coming to court!

sentences.zh: 朕今於便殿待卿，可暫入相見。」

translations.literal: I now await you in the side hall; you may enter briefly to see me."
translations.idiomatic: I am waiting for you in the side hall—come in for a short audience."

sentences.zh: 谷入見於金祥殿，面陳悃款，帝不許。

translations.literal: Gu entered audience at the Jinxiang Hall, stated his sincere intent in person, and the emperor would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Gu came in at Jinxiang Hall and pleaded his case in person, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 谷不得已復視事。

translations.literal: Gu had no choice but to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had no choice but to return to office.

sentences.zh: 谷未能執筆，詔以三司務繁，令刻名印用之。

translations.literal: Gu could not hold a brush. An edict noted that the Three Departments' business was heavy and ordered a carved name seal made for his use.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to write, Gu was authorized by edict—given the press of fiscal affairs—to use an engraved name seal instead.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，敕：「民有訴訟，必先歷縣州及觀察使處決，不直，乃聽詣台省，或自不能書牒，倩人書者，必書所倩姓名、居處。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an edict proclaimed: "When the people have lawsuits, they must first pass through the county, prefecture, and surveillance commissioner for judgment. If the ruling is unjust, only then may they go to the central ministries. If they cannot write the petition themselves and employ another to write it, the name and residence of the person employed must be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict declared: "Litigants must first seek judgment at county, prefecture, and surveillance commissioner levels; only if wronged may they appeal to the central ministries. Anyone who cannot write a petition and hires another must record that person's name and address.

sentences.zh: 若無可倩，聽執素紙。

translations.literal: If there is no one to employ, they may present plain paper.
translations.idiomatic: If no one can be hired, they may submit a blank sheet.

sentences.zh: 所訴必須己事，毋得挾私客訴。」

translations.literal: The complaint must concern one's own affair; private proxies may not lodge suits."
translations.idiomatic: Complaints must concern one's own case; no one may bring suit on another's behalf as a hired agent."

sentences.zh: 慶州刺史郭彥欽性貪，野雞族多羊馬，彥欽故擾之以求賂，野雞族遂反，剽掠綱商。

translations.literal: Guo Yanqin, Prefect of Qingzhou, was greedy by nature. The Yejizu had many sheep and horses; Yanqin deliberately harassed them to extort bribes, and the Yejizu thereupon rebelled and plundered tax convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yanqin, prefect of Qingzhou, was grasping; the Yejizu tribes held large herds, and Yanqin deliberately provoked them for bribes until they rose up and raided tax transports.

sentences.zh: 帝命寧、環二州合兵討之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ning and Huan prefectures to combine forces to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the prefectures of Ning and Huan to join forces and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 劉言遣使奉表來告，稱：「湖南世事朝廷，不幸為鄰寇所陷，臣雖不奉詔，輒糾合義兵，削平舊國。」

translations.literal: Liu Yan sent envoys with a memorial reporting: "Hunan has long served the court. Unhappily it was seized by a neighboring foe. Though I received no imperial command, I have mustered righteous troops and pacified the old domain."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan sent envoys with a memorial stating: "Hunan has always served the dynasty; when a neighboring enemy seized it, I—though without imperial orders—raised loyal troops and restored our former realm."

sentences.zh: 唐主削邊鎬官爵，流饒州。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler stripped Bian Hao of rank and office and banished him to Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler stripped Bian Hao of rank and banished him to Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，鎬以都虞候從查文徽克建州，凡所俘獲皆全之，建人謂之「邊佛子」；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao followed Zha Wenhui as deputy commander to capture Jianzhou, he spared all captives, and the people of Jian called him "Bian the Buddha's Son";
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as deputy commander under Zha Wenhui at the capture of Jianzhou, he spared every captive, and the Jian people called him "Bian the Buddha's son";

sentences.zh: 及克潭州，市不易肆，潭人謂之「邊菩薩」；

translations.literal: when he took Tanzhou the markets did not change their stalls, and the people of Tan called him "Bian the Bodhisattva";
translations.idiomatic: when he took Tanzhou commerce went on undisturbed, and the Tan people called him "Bian the bodhisattva";

sentences.zh: 既而為節度使，政無綱紀，惟日設齋供，盛修佛事，潭人失望，謂之「邊和尚」矣。

translations.literal: later, as military governor, his government had no discipline; he only held daily vegetarian feasts and lavishly performed Buddhist rites. The people of Tan lost hope and called him "Bian the Monk."
translations.idiomatic: but once he became military governor his rule lacked order—he spent his days on vegetarian feasts and grand Buddhist observances—and the Tan people, disillusioned, called him "Bian the monk."

sentences.zh: 左僕射同平章事馮延己、右僕射同平章事孫晟上表請罪，皆釋之。

translations.literal: Feng Yanji, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Sun Sheng, Right Vice Director and Concurrent Grand Councilor, submitted memorials asking punishment; both were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanji, left vice director and grand councilor, and Sun Sheng, right vice director and grand councilor, submitted self-accusations; both were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 晟陳請不已，乃與延己皆罷守本官。

translations.literal: Sheng pressed his plea without cease, and he and Yanji were both dismissed to hold only their original offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng kept pleading his case until he and Yanji were both removed from the grand councilorship and reverted to their original posts.

sentences.zh: 唐主以比年出師無功，乃議休兵息民。

translations.literal: Because campaigns in recent years had achieved nothing, the Tang ruler discussed halting warfare and giving the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: With years of fruitless campaigns behind him, the Tang ruler debated halting war and letting the people recover.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「願陛下數十年不用兵，可小康矣！」

translations.literal: Someone said: "If Your Majesty would refrain from using troops for several decades, modest prosperity could be attained!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "If Your Majesty would go without war for several decades, the realm could know modest ease!"

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「將終身不用，何數十年之有！」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said: "I shall not use them for my whole life—what talk is there of several decades!"
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler replied, "I mean never to use them at all—why speak of mere decades!"

sentences.zh: 唐主思歐陽廣之言，拜本縣令。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler recalled Ouyang Guang's words and appointed him magistrate of his home county.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Ouyang Guang's warning, the Tang ruler appointed him magistrate of his home county.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛未，徙保義節度使折從阮為靜難節度使，討野雞族。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinwei, Zhe Congruan, Military Governor of Baoyi, was transferred to be Military Governor of Jingnan to campaign against the Yejizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinwei, Zhe Congruan was moved from Baoyi to Jingnan military governor to campaign against the Yejizu.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，敕：「約每歲民間所輸牛皮，三分減二；

translations.literal: On guiyou, an edict proclaimed: "Roughly speaking, of the ox hides the people deliver each year, reduce the levy by two-thirds;
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou an edict ordered that the annual ox-hide levy be cut by two-thirds;

sentences.zh: 計田十頃，稅取一皮，餘聽民自用及賣買，惟禁賣於敵國。」

translations.literal: for every ten qing of fields, one hide is taxed; the rest may be used by the people themselves or bought and sold, sale to enemy states alone being forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: one hide per ten qing of land, with the rest free for private use or trade, except sale to enemy states."

sentences.zh: 先是，兵興以來，禁民私賣買牛皮，悉令輸官受直。

translations.literal: Previously, since the rise of warfare, private trade in ox hides had been forbidden; all were to be delivered to the government for payment.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, private trade in hides had been banned and all hides delivered to the state for payment.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗之世，有司止償以鹽；

translations.literal: Under Tang Mingzong, the authorities paid only in salt;
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang Mingzong, officials paid only in salt;

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，並鹽不給。

translations.literal: in Jin's Tianfu era even salt was not given.
translations.idiomatic: under Later Jin's Tianfu reign even salt payments ceased.

sentences.zh: 漢法，犯私牛皮一寸抵死，然民間日用實不可無。

translations.literal: Under Han law, possession of a private ox hide even one inch square was punishable by death, yet in daily life the people truly could not do without them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han law made even a handspan of private hide a capital crime, yet common life could not do without leather.

sentences.zh: 帝素知其弊，至是，李穀建議，均於田畝，公私便之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long known these abuses. At this time Li Gu proposed apportioning the levy by field acreage, to the convenience of public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long known the abuse; now Li Gu proposed apportioning the levy by acreage, to everyone's benefit.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，河決鄭、滑，遣使行視修塞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, the Yellow River burst its banks at Zheng and Hua. Envoys were sent to inspect and repair the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, the Yellow River broke through at Zheng and Hua; envoys were dispatched to inspect and repair the dikes.

sentences.zh: 甲午，前靜難節度使侯章獻買宴絹千匹，銀五百兩。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Hou Zhang, former Military Governor of Jingnan, presented a thousand bolts of silk and five hundred taels of silver to purchase a court feast.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, former Jingnan military governor Hou Zhang offered a thousand bolts of silk and five hundred taels of silver to pay for a court banquet.

sentences.zh: 帝不受，曰：「諸侯入覲，天子宜有宴犒，豈待買邪！

translations.literal: The emperor would not accept them and said: "When feudatories come to court, the Son of Heaven ought to provide a feast and rewards—must he wait to be paid for them!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, saying, "When lords come to court, the Son of Heaven should host them—why should they have to buy their own feast!

sentences.zh: 自今如此比者，皆勿受。」

translations.literal: From now on, all such offerings are not to be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, nothing of the kind is to be accepted."

sentences.zh: 王逵將兵及洞蠻五萬攻郴州，南漢將潘崇徹救之，遇於蚝石。

translations.literal: Wang Kui led troops and fifty thousand cave barbarians to attack Chenzhou. Pan Chongche, a Southern Han general, came to its relief and met them at Haoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui marched on Chenzhou with his army and fifty thousand tribal allies; Southern Han general Pan Chongche came to relieve the city and met them at Haoshi.

sentences.zh: 崇徹登高望湖南兵，曰：「疲而不整，可破也。」

translations.literal: Chongche climbed high and looked upon the Hunan troops, saying: "They are weary and not in order—they can be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Chongche climbed a height, surveyed the Hunan army, and said, "They are tired and out of formation—we can break them."

sentences.zh: 縱擊，大破之，伏屍八十里。

translations.literal: He loosed an attack and routed them utterly; corpses lay strewn for eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: He charged and shattered them; the dead lay thick for eighty li.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士徐台符請誅誣告李崧者葛延遇及李澄，馮道以為屢更赦，不許。

translations.literal: Xu Taifu, Hanlin Academician, requested execution of Ge Yanyu and Li Cheng, who had falsely accused Li Song. Feng Dao held that amnesties had been repeatedly proclaimed and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Xu Taifu asked that Ge Yanyu and Li Cheng, who had framed Li Song, be put to death; Feng Dao argued that repeated amnesties barred it and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 王峻嘉台符之義，白於帝，癸卯，收延遇、澄，誅之。

translations.literal: Wang Jun admired Taifu's righteousness and reported it to the emperor. On guimao, Yanyu and Cheng were seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun applauded Taifu's stand and told the emperor; on guimao Yanyu and Cheng were arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 劉言表稱潭州殘破，乞移使府治朗州，且請貢獻、賣茶，悉如馬氏故事。

translations.literal: Liu Yan memorialized that Tanzhou was devastated and begged to move the commissionerate to Langzhou, and also requested tribute and tea sales all on the former Ma model.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan reported Tanzhou in ruins and asked to move his headquarters to Langzhou, with tribute and tea sales on the old Ma Chu terms.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 唐江西觀察使楚王馬希萼入朝，唐主留之，後數年，卒於金陵，謚曰恭孝。

translations.literal: Ma Xie, Prince of Chu and Jiangxi Surveillance Commissioner of Tang, came to court. The Tang ruler detained him. Several years later he died at Jinling; his posthumous title was Gongxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie, Prince of Chu and Tang surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi, came to court and was kept there; he died at Jinling some years later with the posthumous name Gongxiao.

sentences.zh: 初，麟州土豪楊信自為刺史，受命於周。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Xin, a local strongman of Linzhou, had made himself prefect and received appointment from Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Xin, a local magnate of Linzhou, had made himself prefect with Zhou recognition.

sentences.zh: 信卒，子重訓嗣，以州降北漢。

translations.literal: When Xin died, his son Chongxun succeeded and surrendered the prefecture to Northern Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin died, his son Chongxun succeeded him and surrendered the prefecture to Northern Han.

sentences.zh: 至是，為群羌所圍，復歸款，求救於夏、府二州。

translations.literal: At this time, besieged by various Qiang groups, he renewed submission and sought aid from Xia and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Now, besieged by Qiang tribes, he renewed his allegiance to Zhou and appealed for help to Xia and Fu.

sentences.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武皇帝中廣順三年（

translations.literal: Mid-annals of Taizu the Sagely Divine, Respectful, Solemn, and Martial Cultural Emperor—Guangshun year three (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Central Annals of Emperor Taizu of Later Zhou, Guangshun year three (

sentences.zh: 癸丑，公元九五三年）

translations.literal: Guichou, equivalent to the year 953 CE)
translations.idiomatic: 953 CE, year guichou of the cycle)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙辰，以武平留後劉言為武平節度使，制置武安、靜江等軍事、同平章事；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Liu Yan, Acting Military Governor of Wuping, was appointed Military Governor of Wuping, with authority over Wu'an, Jingjiang, and other military affairs, and Concurrent Grand Councilor;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on bingchen, Liu Yan was made military governor of Wuping, given charge of Wu'an, Jingjiang, and related commands, and named concurrent grand councilor;

sentences.zh: 以王逵為武安節度使，何敬真為靜江節度使，周行逢為武安行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Wang Kui was made Military Governor of Wu'an, He Jingzhen Military Governor of Jingjiang, and Zhou Xingfeng campaigning marshal of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui became military governor of Wu'an, He Jingzhen of Jingjiang, and Zhou Xingfeng campaigning marshal of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 詔折從阮：「野雞族能改過者，拜官賜金帛，不則進兵討之。」

translations.literal: An edict to Zhe Congruan proclaimed: "Among the Yejizu, those who can reform their ways shall receive office and gifts of gold and silk; otherwise advance troops to punish them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Congruan was ordered: "Yejizu who mend their ways shall receive office and rewards; the rest will be attacked."

sentences.zh: 壬戌，從阮奏：「酋長李萬全等受詔立誓外，自餘猶不服，方討之。」

translations.literal: On renxu, Congruan memorialized: "Apart from the chieftains Li Wanquan and others who received the edict and swore oaths, the rest still do not submit and are now being attacked."
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he reported: "Only chieftains such as Li Wanquan who took the oath have submitted; the rest are still being subdued."

sentences.zh: 前世屯田皆在邊地，使戍兵佃之。

translations.literal: In former ages garrison fields were all on the frontier, worked by border troops.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times military colonies lay on the frontier and were farmed by garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 唐末，中原宿兵，所在皆置營田以耕曠土。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, with standing armies throughout the central plain, camp fields were established everywhere to cultivate idle land.
translations.idiomatic: By late Tang, with permanent armies across the heartland, camp farms were set up everywhere to till abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 其後又募高貲戶使輸課佃之，戶部別置官司總領，不隸州縣，或丁多無役，或容庇奸盜，州縣不能詰。

translations.literal: Later wealthy households were recruited to pay dues and farm them. The Revenue Bureau set up a separate office to oversee them, outside county and prefecture control. Some had many adult males yet performed no corvée; others sheltered criminals and bandits, and the counties and prefectures could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Later wealthy tenants were recruited to pay dues and farm the land under a separate Revenue Bureau office outside local government—some evaded labor service, others harbored criminals, and local officials could not check them.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖擊淮南，掠得牛以千萬計，給東南諸州農民，使歲輸租。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu attacked Huainan and seized cattle by the tens of millions, distributing them to farmers in the southeastern prefectures and requiring annual rent payments.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Taizu, campaigning in Huainan, seized millions of cattle, gave them to farmers in the southeast, and required annual rent in return.

sentences.zh: 自是歷數十年，牛死而租不除，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: From this time onward, over the course of several decades, when oxen died the rent was not remitted, and the people suffered greatly from it.
translations.idiomatic: For decades after that, tenants still owed rent even when their oxen died, and the hardship this caused the common people was severe.

sentences.zh: 帝素知其弊，會闔門使、知青州張凝上便宜，請罷營田務，李穀亦以為言。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long known its abuses; it happened that the Gate Commissioner and Qingzhou prefect Zhang Ning submitted a memorial on expedient measures, requesting the abolition of the Farm Offices, and Li Gu also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long been aware of these abuses. Then the Gate Commissioner and Qingzhou prefect Zhang Ning submitted a practical proposal urging that the Farm Offices be abolished, and Li Gu made the same recommendation.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，敕：「悉罷戶部營田務，以其民隸州縣；

translations.literal: On the yichou day, an edict was issued: 'Abolish all Farm Offices under the Ministry of Revenue, and assign their people to the jurisdictions of the prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, an edict declared: 'Abolish every Farm Office under the Ministry of Revenue and place its people under the prefectures and counties;

sentences.zh: 其田、廬、牛、農器，並賜見佃者為永業，悉除租牛課。」

translations.literal: their fields, dwellings, oxen, and farm implements shall all be granted to the current tenants as heritable property in perpetuity, and all ox-rent levies shall be entirely abolished.'
translations.idiomatic: grant the fields, dwellings, oxen, and farm tools to the tenants now working them as permanent heritable property, and abolish all ox-rent taxes entirely.'

sentences.zh: 是歲，戶部增三萬餘戶。

translations.literal: That year, the Ministry of Revenue gained more than thirty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Revenue added more than thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 民既得為永業，始敢葺屋植木，獲地利數倍。

translations.literal: Once the people had obtained heritable rights, they dared at last to repair their houses and plant trees, and the profit they drew from the land increased several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Once the people held secure title to the land, they finally dared to rebuild their homes and plant trees, and their yields from the soil multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 或言：「營田有肥鐃者，不若鬻之，可得錢數十萬緡以資國。」

translations.literal: Someone said: 'Among the farm lands there are fertile and marginal plots; it would be better to sell them, and several hundred thousand strings of cash could be obtained to fund the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Some suggested: 'There are both rich and poor plots among the colony lands—better to sell them and raise several hundred thousand strings of cash for the treasury.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「利在於民，猶在國也，朕用此錢何為！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'When profit rests with the people, it is the same as resting with the state—what would I do with this money!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'When the people prosper, the state prospers too—what use would I have for such money!'

sentences.zh: 萊州刺史葉仁魯，帝之故吏也，坐贓絹萬五千匹，錢千緡。

translations.literal: Ye Renlu, the prefect of Laizhou and a former subordinate of the Emperor, was convicted of corruption involving fifteen thousand bolts of silk and one thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Renlu, prefect of Laizhou and an old retainer of the emperor, was found guilty of embezzling fifteen thousand bolts of silk and one thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賜死。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, he was granted the privilege of death by imperial command.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中使賜以酒食曰：「汝自抵國法，吾無如之何。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent an imperial envoy to grant him wine and food, saying: 'You have brought this upon yourself by violating the laws of the state—I can do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy with wine and a final meal, saying: 'You have violated the law and brought this on yourself; there is nothing I can do.

sentences.zh: 當存恤汝母。」

translations.literal: You should see that your mother is cared for.'
translations.idiomatic: See that your mother is provided for.'

sentences.zh: 仁魯感泣。

translations.literal: Renlu wept with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Renlu wept in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 帝以河決為憂，王峻請自往行視，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled by the breach of the river dikes; Wang Jun requested to go in person to inspect the situation, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply worried about the river breach. Wang Jun asked to go and inspect it himself, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 鎮寧節度使榮屢求入朝，峻忌其英烈，每沮止之。

translations.literal: The Zhenning military commissioner Rong repeatedly requested permission to come to court; Wang Jun envied his heroic reputation and repeatedly obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenning military commissioner Rong repeatedly asked to come to court, but Wang Jun, jealous of his martial renown, blocked him each time.

sentences.zh: 閏月，榮復求入朝，會峻在河上，帝乃許之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Rong again requested to come to court; as it happened Wang Jun was on the river, and the Emperor then granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Rong again petitioned to attend court. Wang Jun happened to be away on the river, and the emperor finally consented.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇定州，圍義豐軍，定和都指揮使楊弘裕夜擊其營，大獲，契丹遁去。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Dingzhou and besieged Yifeng Army; Yang Hongyu, commander of the Dinghe Command, attacked their camp by night, won a great victory, and the Khitan fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan attacked Dingzhou and besieged Yifeng Army. Yang Hongyu, commander of the Dinghe Command, struck their camp at night, won a great victory, and the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又寇鎮州，本道兵擊走之。

translations.literal: They raided Zhenzhou again, and the troops of that circuit drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Zhenzhou again, but the local forces of that circuit beat them back.

sentences.zh: 丙申，鎮寧節度使榮入朝。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, the Zhenning military commissioner Rong came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, the Zhenning military commissioner Rong arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 故李守貞騎士馬全乂從榮入朝，帝召見，補殿前指揮使，謂左右曰：「全乂忠於所事，昔在河中，屢挫吾軍，汝輩宜效之。」

translations.literal: Ma Quanyi, a former cavalryman of Li Shouzhen, accompanied Rong to court. The Emperor summoned and received him, appointing him commander of the Palace Front Corps, and said to those beside him: 'Quanyi was loyal to his master; formerly at Hezhong he repeatedly defeated our army—you all should emulate him.'
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanyi, once a cavalry officer under Li Shouzhen, came to court with Rong. The emperor received him and appointed him commander of the Palace Front Corps, then told his attendants: 'Quanyi was faithful to the lord he served; at Hezhong he repeatedly routed our forces—you would do well to follow his example.'

sentences.zh: 王峻聞榮入朝，遽自河上歸，戊戌，至大梁。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun heard that Rong had come to court, he hurried back from the river; on the wuxu day he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun learned that Rong had entered court, he rushed back from the river and reached Daliang on the wuxu day.

sentences.zh: 雄武節度使高允權卒，其子牙內指揮使紹基謀襲父位，詐稱允權疾病，表己知軍府事。

translations.literal: The Xiongwu military commissioner Gao Yunquan died. His son, the Inner Tooth-guard commander Gao Shaoji, plotted to seize his father's position, falsely claiming that Yunquan was ill and submitting a memorial that he himself was already managing military and administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongwu military commissioner Gao Yunquan died. His son Gao Shaoji, an inner guard commander, plotted to seize his father's post, falsely reporting that Yunquan was ill and that he was already running the command.

sentences.zh: 觀察判官李彬切諫，紹基怒，斬之，辛丑，以彬謀反聞。

translations.literal: The investigation and adjudication official Li Bin remonstrated sharply; Shaoji grew angry and executed him. On the xinchou day, he reported that Bin had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit judge Li Bin urged him forcefully to desist. Shaoji flew into a rage and had him killed. On the xinchou day he reported that Li Bin had plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 王峻固求領籓鎮，帝不得已，壬寅，以峻兼平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Jun persistently requested to hold a frontier command; the Emperor had no choice. On the renyin day, Wang Jun was concurrently appointed Pinglu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun pressed hard for a regional command, and the emperor, unable to refuse, on the renyin day made him concurrent Pinglu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 高紹基屢奏雜虜犯邊，冀得承襲，帝遣六宅使張仁謙詣延州巡檢，紹基不能匿，始發父喪。

translations.literal: Gao Shaoji repeatedly memorialized that various barbarians were raiding the border, hoping thereby to succeed to the post. The Emperor dispatched the Six Residences envoy Zhang Renqian to Yanzhou to inspect; Shaoji could not conceal the matter any longer and at last announced his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shaoji repeatedly reported barbarian raids on the frontier, hoping to secure the succession. The emperor sent the Six Residences envoy Zhang Renqian to Yanzhou to investigate. Unable to hide the truth any longer, Shaoji finally announced his father's death.

sentences.zh: 戊申，折從阮奏降野雞二十一族。

translations.literal: On the wushen day, Zhe Congruan memorialized the surrender of the twenty-one Yaji tribes.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, Zhe Congruan reported that twenty-one Yaji tribes had submitted.

sentences.zh: 唐草澤邵棠上言：「近游淮上，聞周主恭儉，增修德政。

translations.literal: A recluse of Tang, Shao Tang, submitted a memorial saying: 'Recently, while traveling along the Huai River, I heard that the Zhou ruler is respectful and frugal and is increasing and improving virtuous governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Tang, a Tang-era recluse, submitted a memorial: 'I have lately traveled along the Huai and heard that the Zhou ruler is modest and frugal and is steadily improving his rule.

sentences.zh: 吾兵新破於潭、朗，恐其有南征之志，宜為之備。」

translations.literal: Our forces were recently defeated at Tan and Lang; I fear he harbors designs for a southern campaign, and we should make preparations against it.'
translations.idiomatic: Our army was just defeated at Tan and Lang; I fear he intends a southern expedition, and we should prepare against it.'

sentences.zh: 初，王逵既克潭州，以指揮使何敬真為靜江節度副使，朱全琇為武安節度副使，張文表為武平節度副使，周行逢為武安行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Previously, after Wang Kui had taken Tanzhou, he appointed the commander He Jingzhen as deputy military commissioner of Jingjiang, Zhu Quanxiu as deputy military commissioner of Wu'an, Zhang Wenbiao as deputy military commissioner of Wuping, and Zhou Xingfeng as Wu'an army march vice-marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Wang Kui captured Tanzhou, he made the commander He Jingzhen deputy military commissioner of Jingjiang, Zhu Quanxiu deputy military commissioner of Wu'an, Zhang Wenbiao deputy military commissioner of Wuping, and Zhou Xingfeng Wu'an army march vice-marshal.

sentences.zh: 敬真、全琇各置牙兵，與逵分廳視事，吏民莫知所從。

translations.literal: Jingzhen and Quanxiu each maintained their own tooth-guard troops and shared separate halls with Kui in conducting affairs; officials and commoners alike did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen and Quanxiu each kept private guard units and held court in separate halls alongside Kui, so officials and commoners no longer knew whom to obey.

sentences.zh: 每宴集，諸將使酒，紛拿如市，無復上下之分，唯行逢、文表事逵盡禮，逵親愛之。

translations.literal: At every feast and gathering the generals drank freely; the scuffling was like a marketplace, with no distinction between superior and subordinate. Only Xingfeng and Wenbiao served Kui with full propriety, and he favored them dearly.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet the generals drank heavily and brawled like a street market, with no regard for rank. Only Xingfeng and Wenbiao treated Kui with proper deference, and he held them in special affection.

sentences.zh: 敬真與逵不協，辭歸朗州，又不能事劉言，與全琇謀作亂。

translations.literal: Jingzhen was at odds with Kui; he resigned and returned to Langzhou, yet he could not serve Liu Yan well either. Together with Quanxiu he plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen fell out with Kui, resigned, and returned to Langzhou, but he could not get along with Liu Yan either; he and Quanxiu then plotted a revolt.

sentences.zh: 言素忌逵之強，疑逵使敬真伺己，將討之，逵聞之，甚懼。

translations.literal: Yan had long resented Kui's strength, suspected that Kui had sent Jingzhen to spy on him, and was about to move against him. When Kui heard of this, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan had long resented Kui's power and suspected that Kui had posted Jingzhen to watch him; he was preparing to strike back. When Kui heard of it, he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 行逢曰：「劉言素不與吾輩同心，何敬真、朱全琇恥在公下，公宜早圖之。」

translations.literal: Xingfeng said: 'Liu Yan has never been of one mind with us; He Jingzhen and Zhu Quanxiu are ashamed to serve under you—you should deal with them early.'
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng said: 'Liu Yan has never truly stood with us, and He Jingzhen and Zhu Quanxiu chafe at serving beneath you. You should move against them soon.'

sentences.zh: 逵喜曰：「與公共除凶黨，同治潭、朗，夫復何憂！」

translations.literal: Kui said with pleasure: 'Together with you I will eliminate this evil faction and jointly govern Tan and Lang—what further worry could there be!'
translations.idiomatic: Kui said delightedly: 'With you I will wipe out these villains and rule Tan and Lang together—what else is there to fear!'

sentences.zh: 會南漢寇全、道、永州，行逢請：「身至朗州說言，遣敬真、全琇南討，俟至長沙，以計取之，如掌中物耳。」

translations.literal: It happened that Southern Han raided Quan, Dao, and Yong prefectures. Xingfeng requested: 'Let me go in person to Langzhou to persuade Yan; send Jingzhen and Quanxiu south to suppress the enemy. Once they reach Changsha, seize them by stratagem—as easy as taking something from the palm of one's hand.'
translations.idiomatic: Just then Southern Han attacked Quan, Dao, and Yong. Xingfeng proposed: 'Let me go to Langzhou and win Liu Yan over; send Jingzhen and Quanxiu south against the invaders. When they reach Changsha, we can take them by trickery—as easily as grasping something in the palm of the hand.'

sentences.zh: 逵從之。

translations.literal: Kui agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Kui agreed.

sentences.zh: 行逢至朗州，言以敬真為南面行營招討使，全琇為先鋒使，將牙兵百餘人會潭州兵以御南漢。

translations.literal: Xingfeng reached Langzhou. Yan appointed Jingzhen commander of the southern campaign headquarters and Quanxiu vanguard commander, and they led more than a hundred tooth-guard troops to join the Tanzhou forces in resisting Southern Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng reached Langzhou. Liu Yan made Jingzhen commander of the southern campaign headquarters and Quanxiu vanguard commander; they took more than a hundred guard troops and joined the Tanzhou army to repel Southern Han.

sentences.zh: 二人至長沙，逵出郊迎，相見甚歡，宴飲連日，多以美妓餌之，敬真因淹留不進。

translations.literal: When the two men reached Changsha, Kui went out to the suburbs to welcome them. Their meeting was very joyous; they feasted and drank for days on end, and he largely offered them beautiful courtesans as bait. Jingzhen therefore lingered and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the two arrived at Changsha, Kui went out to meet them in the suburbs. They greeted each other warmly and feasted for days on end, Kui plying them with beautiful entertainers. Jingzhen lingered and would not march on.

sentences.zh: 朗州指揮使李仲遷部兵三千人久戍潭州，敬真使之先發，趣嶺北，都頭符會等因士卒思歸，劫仲遷擅還朗州。

translations.literal: The Langzhou commander Li Zhongqian had long garrisoned Tanzhou with three thousand troops under his command. Jingzhen had them set out first, pressing toward the north of the Ling Mountains. The platoon leaders Fu Hui and others, because the soldiers longed to return home, seized Zhongqian and forcibly returned to Langzhou on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongqian, the Langzhou commander, had long kept three thousand men on garrison duty at Tanzhou. Jingzhen ordered them to march first toward the north of the Ling range. But the squad leaders Fu Hui and others, seeing how badly the men wanted to go home, seized Zhongqian and marched back to Langzhou on their own.

sentences.zh: 逵乘敬真醉，使人詐為言使者，責敬真以「南寇深侵，不亟捍御而專務荒宴，太師命械公歸西府。」

translations.literal: Taking advantage of Jingzhen's drunkenness, Kui sent someone posing as an envoy from Yan to accuse Jingzhen: 'The southern invaders have penetrated deeply; instead of defending at once you devote yourself to wasteful revelry. The Grand Preceptor orders you shackled and returned to the western headquarters.'
translations.idiomatic: While Jingzhen was drunk, Kui sent a man disguised as an envoy from Liu Yan to denounce him: 'The southern enemy has driven deep into our territory, yet you indulge in feasting instead of defending the border. The Grand Preceptor orders you bound and sent back to the western headquarters.'

sentences.zh: 因收繫獄。

translations.literal: He was thereupon arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 全琇逃去，遣兵追捕之。

translations.literal: Quanxiu fled; troops were dispatched to pursue and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanxiu escaped, and Kui sent troops to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛亥朔，斬敬真以徇。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the cycle, xinhai, Jingzhen was beheaded as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day, xinhai, Jingzhen was executed as a public example.

sentences.zh: 未幾，獲全琇及其黨十餘人，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Before long, Quanxiu and more than ten of his followers were captured, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Quanxiu and more than ten of his accomplices were captured and all were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，鎮寧節度使榮歸澶州。

translations.literal: On the guichou day, the Zhenning military commissioner Rong returned to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day, the Zhenning military commissioner Rong returned to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主德光北還，以晉傳國寶自隨。

translations.literal: Previously, when the Khitan emperor Deguang returned north, he took with him the Jin dynastic imperial seals of succession.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Khitan emperor Deguang withdrew northward, he carried off the Jin dynasty's imperial seals of transmission.

sentences.zh: 至是，更以玉作二寶。

translations.literal: At this time, two new seals were fashioned from jade.
translations.idiomatic: Now, two new imperial seals were carved from jade.

sentences.zh: 王逵遣使以斬何敬真告劉言，言不得己，庚申，斬符會等數人。

translations.literal: Wang Kui sent envoys to report to Liu Yan that He Jingzhen had been executed; Yan had no choice; on gengshen day, Fu Hui and several others were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui sent messengers to inform Liu Yan of He Jingzhen's execution. Left with no alternative, Liu Yan, on the gengshen day, had Fu Hui and several others put to death.

sentences.zh: 樞密使、平盧節度使、同平章事王峻，晚節益狂躁，奏請以端明殿學士顏衎、樞密直學士陳觀代范質、李穀為相，帝曰：「進退宰輔，不可倉猝，俟朕更思之。」

translations.literal: Wang Jun, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Military Governor of Pinglu, and Co-Head of the Secretariat, in his later years grew ever more arrogant and rash; he memorialized asking that Academician of the Hall of Illuminated Excellence Yan Kan and Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs Chen Guan replace Fan Zhi and Li Gu as chief ministers. The Emperor said: "The appointment and dismissal of chief ministers must not be done in haste; let me consider the matter further."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun—Commissioner of Military Affairs, Military Governor of Pinglu, and Co-Head of the Secretariat—in his later years grew increasingly arrogant and volatile. He memorialized the throne, proposing that Yan Kan and Chen Guan replace Fan Zhi and Li Gu as chief ministers. The Emperor replied, "The appointment and removal of chief ministers is not a matter to be decided in haste. I must think on it further."

sentences.zh: 峻力論列，語浸不遜，日向中，帝尚未食，峻爭之不已。

translations.literal: Jun argued forcefully at length; his words gradually became disrespectful; the sun had reached midday and the Emperor had still not eaten, yet Jun continued pressing his argument without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Jun pressed his case relentlessly, his language growing ever more insubordinate. The sun stood at noon and the Emperor had still not eaten, yet Jun would not let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今方寒食，俟假開，如卿所奏。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "It is now the Cold Food Festival; wait until the holiday ends, then do as you have memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "It is the Cold Food Festival—wait until the holiday ends, then proceed as you have proposed."

sentences.zh: 峻乃退。

translations.literal: Jun then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Jun withdraw.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝函召宰相、樞密使入，幽峻於別所。

translations.literal: On guihai day, the Emperor secretly summoned the chief ministers and the Commissioner of Military Affairs; Wang Jun was confined in a separate place.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day, the Emperor secretly summoned the chief ministers and the Commissioner of Military Affairs. Wang Jun was sequestered elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 帝見馮道等，泣曰：「王峻陵朕太甚，欲盡逐大臣，翦朕羽翼。

translations.literal: The Emperor met Feng Dao and the others and, weeping, said: "Wang Jun has treated me with excessive insolence; he wishes to drive out all the ministers and cut away my wings.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Feng Dao and the others, the Emperor wept and said, "Wang Jun has treated me with intolerable contempt. He wants to drive out every minister and strip me of my wings.

sentences.zh: 朕惟一子，專務間阻，暫令詣闕，已懷怨望。

translations.literal: I have only one son, yet he has deliberately worked to obstruct us; though I briefly summoned him to court, he already harbors resentment and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: I have but one son, yet Jun has gone out of his way to come between us. Though I briefly summoned him to court, he already nurses resentment and disaffection.

sentences.zh: 豈有身典樞機，復兼宰相，又求重鎮！

translations.literal: How can one man hold the keys to military affairs, also serve as chief minister, and yet demand a major military governorship as well!
translations.idiomatic: What man holds the reins of military affairs, serves concurrently as chief minister, and still demands a major commandery besides!

sentences.zh: 觀其志趣，殊未盈厭。

translations.literal: Looking at his ambitions, he is far from satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by his ambitions, he is nowhere near sated.

sentences.zh: 無君如此，誰則堪之！」

translations.literal: To behave toward one's sovereign in such a manner—who could tolerate it!"
translations.idiomatic: To show such contempt for one's sovereign—who could endure it!"

sentences.zh: 甲子，貶峻商州司馬，制辭略曰：「肉視群後，孩撫朕躬。」

translations.literal: On jiazi day, Wang Jun was demoted to Military Assistant of Shangzhou; the edict in part read: "He regarded the assembled officials as mere flesh; he handled me as one would an infant."
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, Wang Jun was demoted to Military Assistant of Shangzhou. The edict read, in part: "He looked upon the court as so much meat, and treated my person as a child to be handled at will."

sentences.zh: 帝慮鄴都留守王殷不自安，命殷子尚食使承誨詣殷，諭以峻得罪之狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor, fearing that Wang Yin, Military Governor of Ye, might feel uneasy, ordered Yin's son, Imperial Food Commissioner Chenghui, to go to Yin and explain the circumstances of Wang Jun's disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Wang Yin, Military Governor of Ye, might grow anxious, the Emperor sent Yin's son Chenghui, Commissioner of Imperial Provisions, to explain what had befallen Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 峻至商州，得腹疾，帝猶愍之，命其妻往視之，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: When Jun reached Shangzhou he contracted a stomach ailment; the Emperor still felt pity for him and ordered his wife to go and attend to him; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fell ill with a stomach disorder after reaching Shangzhou. The Emperor still felt compassion for him and sent his wife to care for him, but before long Jun was dead.

sentences.zh: 帝命折從阮分兵屯延州，高紹基始懼，屢有貢獻。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhe Congruan to divide his forces and garrison Yanzhou; Gao Shaoji only then became fearful and repeatedly sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Zhe Congruan to detach troops and garrison Yanzhou. Only then did Gao Shaoji grow alarmed and begin sending tribute repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 又命供奉官張懷貞將禁兵兩指揮屯鄜、延，紹基乃悉以軍府事授副使張匡圖。

translations.literal: The Emperor also ordered Palace Attendant Zhang Huaizhen to lead two commands of the Imperial Guard to garrison at Fu and Yan; Shaoji then entrusted all military and administrative affairs to his deputy Zhang Kuangtu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor further ordered Palace Attendant Zhang Huaizhen to lead two commands of the Imperial Guard to garrison Fu and Yan. Shaoji thereupon handed over all military and administrative affairs to his deputy, Zhang Kuangtu.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以客省使向訓權知延州。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day, Guest Hall Commissioner Xiang Xun was appointed acting prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day, Guest Reception Commissioner Xiang Xun was appointed acting prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲申，以鎮寧節度使榮為開封尹、晉王。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiashen day, Military Governor of Zhenning Rong was made Prefect of Kaifeng and Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiashen day, Chai Rong, Military Governor of Zhenning, was appointed Prefect of Kaifeng and Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以樞密副使鄭仁誨為鎮寧節度使。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs Zheng Renhui was made Military Governor of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day, Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs Zheng Renhui was appointed Military Governor of Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 初，殺牛族與野雞族有隙，聞官軍討野雞，饋餉迎奉，官軍利其財畜而掠之；

translations.literal: Initially the Slaughter-Cattle tribe and the Wild-Pheasant tribe had a feud; hearing that government troops were campaigning against the Wild-Pheasant tribe, the Slaughter-Cattle tribe sent provisions and welcomed them, but the government troops coveted their wealth and livestock and plundered them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Slaughter-Cattle and Wild-Pheasant tribes had been at odds. When the Slaughter-Cattle heard that imperial troops were campaigning against the Wild-Pheasant, they sent supplies and welcomed the army—only for the troops to covet their wealth and livestock and plunder them.

sentences.zh: 殺牛族反，與野雞合，敗寧州刺史張建武於包山。

translations.literal: The Slaughter-Cattle tribe rebelled, joined with the Wild-Pheasant tribe, and defeated Prefect of Ningzhou Zhang Jianwu at Mount Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The Slaughter-Cattle rose in revolt, joined forces with the Wild-Pheasant, and routed Ningzhou Prefect Zhang Jianwu at Mount Bao.

sentences.zh: 帝以郭彥欽擾群胡，致其作亂，黜廢於家。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that Guo Yanqin had harassed the various Hu tribes and caused them to rebel; he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor blamed Guo Yanqin for harassing the frontier tribes and provoking their rebellion, and dismissed him to his home.

sentences.zh: 初，解州刺史浚儀郭元昭與榷鹽使李溫玉有隙，溫玉婿魏仁浦為樞密主事，元昭疑仁浦庇之。

translations.literal: Initially, Prefect of Jiezhou Guo Yuanzhao of Junyi and Salt Monopoly Commissioner Li Wenyu had a feud; Wenyu's son-in-law Wei Renpu served as a clerical officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Yuanzhao suspected Renpu of shielding him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiezhou Prefect Guo Yuanzhao of Junyi and Salt Monopoly Commissioner Li Wenyu had fallen out. Wenyu's son-in-law Wei Renpu served as a staff officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Yuanzhao suspected that Renpu was protecting him.

sentences.zh: 會李守貞反，溫玉有子在河中，元昭收系溫玉，奏言其叛，事連仁浦。

translations.literal: When Li Shouzhen rebelled, Wenyu had a son in Hezhong; Yuanzhao arrested and detained Wenyu, memorialized that he had rebelled, and implicated Renpu in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shouzhen rebelled, Wenyu happened to have a son in Hezhong. Yuanzhao arrested Wenyu, memorialized that he had joined the rebellion, and implicated Renpu as well.

sentences.zh: 帝時為樞密使，知其誣，釋不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then Commissioner of Military Affairs; knowing it was a false accusation, he released them and took no action.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then Commissioner of Military Affairs. Recognizing the charge as false, he released the men and pursued the matter no further.

sentences.zh: 至是，仁浦為樞密承旨，元昭代歸，甚懼，過洛陽，以告仁浦弟仁滌，仁滌曰：「吾兄平生不與人為怨，況肯以私害公乎！」

translations.literal: By this time Renpu had become Chief Secretary of Military Affairs; Yuanzhao was returning after being replaced and was greatly afraid; passing through Luoyang, he told Renpu's younger brother Rendi, who said: "My elder brother has never borne ill will toward anyone in his life—how would he use personal grievance to harm public duty!"
translations.idiomatic: By now Wei Renpu had risen to Chief Secretary of Military Affairs. Yuanzhao, replaced and returning home, was deeply afraid. Passing through Luoyang, he confided in Renpu's younger brother Rendi. Rendi said, "My brother has never made an enemy in his life—why would he let private grievance corrupt public duty!"

sentences.zh: 既至，丁亥，仁浦白帝，以元昭為慶州刺史。

translations.literal: When he arrived, on dinghai day, Renpu reported to the Emperor and Yuanzhao was appointed Prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his arrival, on dinghai day, Renpu informed the Emperor, and Yuanzhao was appointed Prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以棣州團練使太原王仁鎬為宣徽北院使兼樞密副使

translations.literal: On jichou day, Military Training Commissioner of Dizhou Wang Renhao of Taiyuan was made Commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Domestic Service and concurrently Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day, Wang Renhao of Taiyuan, Military Training Commissioner of Dizhou, was appointed Commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Domestic Service and concurrently Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 唐主復以左僕射馮延己同平章事。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler again appointed Left Vice Director Feng Yanji as Co-Head of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Tang again appointed Left Vice Director Feng Yanji Co-Head of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周行逢惡武平節度副使張仿，言於王逵曰：「何敬真，仿之親戚，臨刑以後事屬仿，公宜備之。」

translations.literal: Zhou Xingfeng bore hatred toward Deputy Military Governor of Wuping Zhang Fang and said to Wang Kui: "He Jingzhen was Fang's kinsman; on the eve of execution he entrusted his affairs to Fang—my lord ought to be on guard."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng hated Zhang Fang, Deputy Military Governor of Wuping, and told Wang Kui, "He Jingzhen was Fang's kinsman. Before his execution he entrusted his affairs to Fang. My lord should be on guard."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚申，逵召仿飲，醉而殺之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on gengshen day, Kui summoned Fang to drink, got him drunk, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengshen day, Kui invited Fang to drink, got him drunk, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，歸德節度使兼侍中常思入朝，戊辰，徙平盧節度使。

translations.literal: On bingyin day, Military Governor of Guide and Palace Secretary Chang Si came to court; on wuchen day he was transferred to Military Governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day, Chang Si, Military Governor of Guide and Palace Secretary, arrived at court. On wuchen day he was transferred to Military Governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 將行，奏曰：「臣在宋州，舉絲四萬餘兩在民間，謹以上進，請征之。」

translations.literal: Before departing, he memorialized: "While I was at Songzhou, I advanced more than forty thousand taels of silk among the people; I respectfully report this above and request permission to collect it."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, he memorialized, "While serving at Songzhou, I advanced more than forty thousand taels of silk among the people. I respectfully report this and request permission to collect it."

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor nodded in assent.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁亥，敕榜宋州，凡常思所舉絲悉蠲之，已輸者復歸之，思亦無怍色。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dinghai day, an edict was posted at Songzhou: all silk that Chang Si had advanced was entirely remitted; what had already been paid in was returned; Si showed no sign of shame either.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dinghai day, an edict was posted at Songzhou remitting every tael of silk Chang Si had advanced, and ordering repayment to those who had already paid. Chang Si showed not the slightest embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 自唐末以來，所在學校廢絕，蜀毋昭裔出私財百萬營學館，且請刻板印《九經》。

translations.literal: Since the end of the Tang, schools everywhere had been abandoned; in Shu, Wu Zhaoyi spent a million in private funds to establish an academy and requested that woodblocks be carved to print the Nine Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late Tang, schools had fallen into ruin everywhere. In Shu, Wu Zhaoyi spent a million in private wealth to build an academy and petitioned to have woodblocks carved for printing the Nine Classics.

sentences.zh: 蜀主從之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Shu granted his request.

sentences.zh: 由是蜀中文學復盛。

translations.literal: From this, letters and learning in Shu flourished once again.
translations.idiomatic: From that time, letters and learning in Shu flourished anew.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，滄州奏契丹知戶台軍事范陽張藏英來降。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renzi day, Cangzhou reported that Zhang Cangying of Fanyang, who managed military affairs at Hutai for the Khitan, had come to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi day, Cangzhou reported that Zhang Cangying of Fanyang, the Khitan officer in charge of military affairs at Hutai, had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，唐明宗之世，宰相馮道、李愚請令判國子監田敏校正《九經》，刻板印賣，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Initially, during the reign of Tang Emperor Mingzong, chief ministers Feng Dao and Li Yu requested that Tian Min, Administrator of the Directorate of Education, be ordered to collate and correct the Nine Classics and have woodblocks carved for printing and sale; the court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the reign of Tang Mingzong, chief ministers Feng Dao and Li Yu petitioned that Tian Min, Administrator of the Directorate of Education, be ordered to collate the Nine Classics and have them carved on woodblocks for printing and sale. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，板成，獻之。

translations.literal: On dingsi day, the blocks were completed and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day the blocks were finished and presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 由是，雖亂世，《九經》傳佈甚廣。

translations.literal: From this, even amid a chaotic age, the Nine Classics spread very widely.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, even in an age of turmoil, the Nine Classics circulated far and wide.

sentences.zh: 王逵以周行逢知潭州，自將兵襲朗州，克之，殺指揮使鄭珓，執武安節度使、同平章事劉言，幽於別館。

translations.literal: Wang Kui put Zhou Xingfeng in charge of Tanzhou, personally led troops to strike Langzhou, captured it, killed Commandant Zheng Yan, seized Military Governor of Wu'an and Co-Head of the Secretariat Liu Yan, and confined him in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui placed Zhou Xingfeng in charge of Tanzhou, then personally led troops in a surprise attack on Langzhou. He took the city, killed Commandant Zheng Yan, seized Liu Yan—Military Governor of Wu'an and Co-Head of the Secretariat—and imprisoned him in a separate lodge.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，王殷三表請入朝，帝疑其不誠，遣使止之。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wang Yin thrice memorialized requesting permission to come to court; the Emperor suspected he was not sincere and sent envoys to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Yin thrice petitioned for permission to come to court. The Emperor doubted his sincerity and sent envoys to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 唐大旱，井泉涸，淮水可涉，饑民度淮而北者相繼，濠、壽發兵御之，民與兵斗而北來。

translations.literal: Tang suffered a great drought; wells and springs dried up, the Huai River could be waded across; starving people crossing the Huai northward came in succession; Hao and Shou sent troops to block them, yet the people fought the soldiers and continued north.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought struck Tang: wells and springs ran dry, and the Huai could be waded on foot. Starving refugees crossed the river northward in an unbroken stream. Hao and Shou dispatched troops to stop them, but the people fought through and kept coming north.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之曰：「彼我之民一也，聽糴米過淮。」

translations.literal: The Emperor heard this and said: "They and our people are one and the same; allow them to purchase grain and cross the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this, he said, "Their people and ours are one and the same. Let them buy grain and cross the Huai."

sentences.zh: 唐人遂築倉，多糴以供軍。

translations.literal: The Tang people then built granaries and bought grain in large quantities to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Tang thereupon built granaries and bought up grain in bulk to supply their army.

sentences.zh: 八月，己未，詔唐民以人畜負米者聽之，以舟車運載者勿予。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiwei day, an edict stated that Tang people carrying grain on their own backs or with pack animals would be permitted, but those transporting it by boat or cart would not be granted passage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiwei day, an edict declared that Tang subjects carrying grain on their backs or with pack animals would be allowed to cross, but those transporting it by boat or cart would not.

sentences.zh: 王逵遣使上表，誣「劉言謀以朗州降唐，又欲攻潭州，其眾不從，廢而囚之，臣已至朗州撫安軍府訖。」

translations.literal: Wang Kui sent envoys submitting a memorial falsely alleging: "Liu Yan plotted to surrender Langzhou to Tang and also intended to attack Tanzhou; his troops would not follow him, so I deposed and imprisoned him; I have already reached Langzhou and pacified the military administration."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui sent envoys with a memorial falsely claiming, "Liu Yan plotted to surrender Langzhou to Tang and also intended to attack Tanzhou. His troops refused to follow him, so I deposed and imprisoned him. I have now reached Langzhou and restored order to the military administration."

sentences.zh: 且請復移使府治潭州。

translations.literal: And he requested that the military commissionerate be moved back to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that the military commissionerate be moved back to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，遣通事舍人翟光裔詣湖南宣撫，從其所請。

translations.literal: On the day Jiaxu, he dispatched the Tongshi Sheren Zhai Guangyi to go to the Hunan pacification commissioner and granted what he had requested.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiaxu, the court sent the diplomatic officer Zhai Guangyi to the Hunan pacification commissioner and approved his request.

sentences.zh: 逵還長沙，以周行逢知朗州事，又遣潘叔嗣殺劉言於朗州。

translations.literal: Kui returned to Changsha, put Zhou Xingfeng in charge of Langzhou affairs, and again sent Pan Shusi to kill Liu Yan in Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kui returned to Changsha, appointed Zhou Xingfeng to administer Langzhou, and sent Pan Shusi to kill Liu Yan there.

sentences.zh: 九月，己亥，武成節度使白重贊奏塞決河。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day Jihai, the Wucheng military governor Bai Chongzan memorialized to block the breached river.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day Jihai, Bai Chongzan, military governor of Wucheng, submitted a memorial calling for the breached Yellow River to be dammed.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇樂壽，齊州戍兵右保寧都頭劉彥章殺都監杜延熙，謀應契丹，不克，並其黨伏誅。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Leshou. Liu Yanzhang, the Right Baoning company head among the garrison troops of Qi Prefecture, killed the overseer Du Yanxi and plotted to join the Khitan. They did not succeed, and he and his followers were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked Leshou, Liu Yanzhang, a company head in the Qi Prefecture garrison, killed the garrison commander Du Yanxi and tried to go over to the Khitan. The plot failed, and he and his accomplices were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 南漢主立其子繼興為衛王，璇興為桂王，慶興為荊王，保興為禎王，崇興為梅王。

translations.literal: The ruler of Southern Han enfeoffed his sons: Jixing as Prince of Wei, Xuanxing as Prince of Gui, Qingxing as Prince of Jing, Baoxing as Prince of Zhen, and Chongxing as Prince of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Southern Han enfeoffed five of his sons: Jixing as Prince of Wei, Xuanxing as Prince of Gui, Qingxing as Prince of Jing, Baoxing as Prince of Zhen, and Chongxing as Prince of Mei.

sentences.zh: 東自青、徐，南至安、復，西至丹、慈，北至貝、鎮，皆大水。

translations.literal: From Qing and Xu in the east, to An and Fu in the south, to Dan and Ci in the west, and to Bei and Zhen in the north, everywhere there was great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: From Qing and Xu in the east to An and Fu in the south, from Dan and Ci in the west to Bei and Zhen in the north, the whole region was stricken by severe floods.

sentences.zh: 帝自入秋得風痺疾，害於食飲及步趨，術者言宜散財以禳之。

translations.literal: Since entering autumn the emperor had contracted a wind-paralysis illness that harmed his eating, drinking, and walking. Magicians said he should disburse wealth to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: After autumn set in, the emperor fell ill with a paralytic condition that impaired his eating, drinking, and walking. Soothsayers advised that he should give away wealth to dispel the affliction.

sentences.zh: 帝欲祀南郊，又以自梁以來，郊祀常在洛陽，疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to sacrifice at the southern suburb, but since the Liang dynasty suburban sacrifices had usually been held at Luoyang, he was uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to perform the southern suburban sacrifice, but because such rites had customarily been held at Luoyang since the Liang dynasty, he was unsure whether he should do so.

sentences.zh: 執政曰：「天子所都則可以祀百神，何必洛陽！」

translations.literal: Those in power said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven makes his capital, he may sacrifice to the hundred spirits—why must it be Luoyang!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven makes his capital, he may sacrifice to all the gods—why must it be Luoyang?"

sentences.zh: 於是，始築圜丘、社稷壇，作太廟於大梁。

translations.literal: Thereupon they first built the Round Mound and the altars of soil and grain, and constructed the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, they built the Round Mound and the altars of soil and grain, and established the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，遣馮道迎太廟社稷神主於洛陽。

translations.literal: On the day Guihai, he dispatched Feng Dao to welcome the spirit tablets of the Imperial Temple and the altars of soil and grain from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guihai, the court sent Feng Dao to Luoyang to bring back the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 南漢大赦。

translations.literal: Southern Han issued a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Han proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，己丑，太常請准洛陽築四郊諸壇，從之。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Jichou, the Director of Ceremonies requested permission to build the altars of the four suburbs according to the Luoyang model, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day Jichou, the Director of Ceremonies asked to build the four suburban altars on the Luoyang model, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁未朔，神主至大梁，帝迎於西郊，祔享於太廟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day Dingwei, the spirit tablets reached Daliang. The emperor received them at the western suburb and enshrined them in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day Dingwei, the spirit tablets arrived at Daliang. The emperor received them at the western suburb and installed them in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 鄴都留守、天雄節度使兼侍衛親軍都指揮使、同平章事王殷恃功專橫，凡河北鎮戍兵應用敕處分者，殷即以帖行之，又多掊斂民財。

translations.literal: Wang Yin, garrison commander of Ye, military governor of Tianxiong, concurrently commander of the Palace Guard, and co–Grand Councilor, relied on his merits to act arbitrarily and domineeringly. Whenever Hebei garrison troops required disposition by imperial edict, Yin would carry it out on his own authority with a written order, and he also greatly extorted the people's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, who held Ye as garrison commander and Tianxiong as military governor while also commanding the Palace Guard and serving as co–Grand Councilor, grew arrogant on the strength of his achievements. Whenever Hebei garrison forces were supposed to be moved by imperial edict, he issued orders on his own authority instead, and he also extorted large sums from the people.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之不悅，使人謂曰：「卿與國同體，鄴都帑庾甚豐，卿欲用則取之，何患無財！」

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and was displeased. He sent someone to say to him, "You and the state are one body. The treasury at Ye is very rich. If you wish to use funds, take them—why worry about lacking money!"
