translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and was displeased. He sent a messenger to tell him, "You and the state are one and the same. Ye's treasury is abundantly stocked—take what you need from it. Why must you worry about money?"

sentences.zh: 成德節度使何福進素惡殷，甲子，福進入朝，密以殷陰事白帝，帝由是疑之。

translations.literal: He Fujin, military governor of Chengde, had long hated Yin. On the day Jiazi, Fujin entered court and secretly reported Yin's hidden misdeeds to the emperor, and the emperor thereby grew suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: He Fujin, military governor of Chengde, had long despised Wang Yin. On the day Jiazi, Fujin came to court and secretly informed the emperor of Yin's misconduct, and from that point the emperor began to distrust him.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，殷入朝，詔留殷充京城內外巡檢。

translations.literal: On the day Yichou, Yin entered court, and an edict retained him to serve as inspector of the capital, inside and outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yichou, Wang Yin came to court, and an edict was issued keeping him in the capital as inspector of the city, both within and beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，府州防禦使折德扆奏北漢將喬贇入寇，擊走之。

translations.literal: On the day Wuchen, Zhe Deyi, defense commissioner of Fuzhou, reported that the Northern Han general Qiao Yun had invaded, and that he had beaten him back.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuchen, Zhe Deyi, defense commissioner of Fuzhou, reported that the Northern Han general Qiao Yun had raided the border and that he had driven the invaders off.

sentences.zh: 王殷每出入，從者常數百人。

translations.literal: Whenever Wang Yin went out or came in, his followers regularly numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wang Yin went out or returned, he was accompanied by several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 殷請量給鎧仗以備巡邏，帝難之。

translations.literal: Yin requested a measured allotment of armor and weapons to prepare for patrol and inspection, and the emperor found this difficult to grant.
translations.idiomatic: Yin asked for a fixed allotment of armor and weapons for his patrol duties, but the emperor was reluctant to grant it.

sentences.zh: 時帝體不平，將行郊祀，而殷挾震主之勢在左右，眾心忌之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's health was poor and he was about to perform the suburban sacrifice, while Yin, wielding the aura of one who awes his ruler, remained at his side, and everyone resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then in poor health and about to perform the suburban sacrifice, while Yin stayed constantly at his side with the overbearing air of a man who intimidated his sovereign, and many grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 壬申，帝力疾御滋德殿，殷入起居，遂執之。

translations.literal: On the day Renshen, the emperor, forcing himself despite illness, held court at Zide Hall. Yin came in to inquire after his health, and was immediately seized.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renshen, the emperor, though seriously ill, held audience in Zide Hall. When Yin came in to pay his respects, he was seized on the spot.

sentences.zh: 下制誣殷謀以郊祀日作亂，流登州，出城，殺之，命鎮寧節度使鄭仁誨詣鄴都安撫。

translations.literal: An edict was issued falsely charging Yin with plotting rebellion on the day of the suburban sacrifice. He was exiled to Dengzhou, and once outside the city he was killed. The emperor ordered Zheng Renhui, military governor of Zhenning, to go to Ye to restore order.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued falsely accusing Yin of plotting a rebellion on the day of the suburban sacrifice. He was sentenced to exile in Dengzhou, but was killed outside the city on the way. The court then ordered Zheng Renhui, military governor of Zhenning, to go to Ye and restore calm.

sentences.zh: 仁誨利殷家財，擅殺殷子，遷其家屬於登州。

translations.literal: Renhui coveted Yin's family wealth, killed Yin's son on his own authority, and relocated his family members to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renhui coveted the Wang family's wealth, had Yin's son killed without authorization, and sent the rest of the family into exile at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐祠部朗中、知制誥徐鉉言貢舉初設，不宜遽罷，乃復行之。

translations.literal: Xu Xuan of Tang, a director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts, said that since the civil service examination had only just been established, it should not be hastily abolished, and so it was resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan, a director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts under Tang, argued that because the civil service examination had only recently been instituted, it should not be abolished so soon, and the examinations were therefore restored.

sentences.zh: 先是，楚州刺史田敬洙請修白水塘溉田以實邊，馮延己以為便。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tian Jingzhu, prefect of Chuzhou, had requested repairing Baishui Pond to irrigate fields and strengthen the border, and Feng Yanji thought this advisable.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tian Jingzhu, prefect of Chuzhou, had proposed repairing Baishui Pond to irrigate farmland and strengthen the frontier, and Feng Yanji had approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 李德明因請大辟曠土為屯田，修復所在渠塘堙廢者。

translations.literal: Li Deming thereupon requested broadly opening idle land for military colonies and restoring silted and abandoned canals and ponds wherever they were found.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deming then proposed opening large tracts of unused land for military farming colonies and restoring canals and ponds that had silted up or fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 吏因緣侵擾，大興力役，奪民田甚眾，民愁怨無訴。

translations.literal: Officials used the opportunity to encroach and harass, launched major corvée labor projects, and seized a great deal of farmland from the people. The people grieved and resented this but had no one to whom they could appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Officials took the opportunity to abuse their power, launched massive forced-labor projects, and seized large amounts of farmland from the people, who grew bitter and resentful but had no recourse.

sentences.zh: 徐鉉以白唐主，唐主命鉉按視之，鉉籍民田悉歸其主。

translations.literal: Xu Xuan reported this to the ruler of Tang, who ordered Xu to investigate. Xu registered the farmland and returned it all to its owners.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan reported the matter to the Tang ruler, who ordered him to inspect the project. Xu reviewed the land records and returned all seized fields to their rightful owners.

sentences.zh: 或譖鉉擅作威福，唐主怒，流鉉舒州。

translations.literal: Some slandered Xu for arrogating authority and making arbitrary decisions. The Tang ruler was angry and exiled Xu to Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials accused Xu of abusing his authority, and the Tang ruler, enraged, banished him to Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 然白水塘竟不成。

translations.literal: Yet Baishui Pond was never completed after all.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, however, Baishui Pond was never completed.

sentences.zh: 唐主又命少府監馮延魯巡撫諸州，右拾遺徐鍇表延魯無才多罪，舉措輕淺，不宜奉使。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler also ordered Feng Yanlu, director of the Palace Workshops, to tour and inspect the prefectures. The Right Reminder Xu Kai memorialized that Yanlu lacked talent and had many offenses, that his conduct was shallow and reckless, and that he was unfit to serve as an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler also appointed Feng Yanlu, director of the Palace Workshops, to tour and inspect the prefectures. Xu Kai, a Right Reminder, submitted a memorial stating that Yanlu was incompetent, guilty of many offenses, and too rash and shallow in his actions to serve as an imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 唐主怒，貶鍇校書郎、分司東都。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was angry and demoted Kai to proofreader, assigning him to the eastern capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler was furious and demoted Kai to the post of proofreader in the eastern capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 鍇，鉉之弟也。

translations.literal: Kai was Xu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was Xu Xuan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 道州盤容洞蠻酋盤崇聚眾自稱盤容州都統，屢寇郴、道州。

translations.literal: Pan Chong, a Miao chieftain of Panrong Cave in Daozhou, gathered followers and styled himself commander-in-chief of Panrong Prefecture, repeatedly raiding Chen and Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Chong, a tribal chieftain of Panrong Cave in Daozhou, gathered a following, declared himself commander-in-chief of Panrong Prefecture, and repeatedly attacked Chen and Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，帝朝享太廟，被兗冕，左右掖以登階，才及一室，酌獻，俯首不能拜而退，命晉王榮終禮。

translations.literal: On the day Yihai, the emperor performed the morning sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Wearing ceremonial robes and cap, he was supported on both sides up the steps. He reached only one chamber, poured the libation, and when he bowed his head he could not complete the bow and withdrew. He ordered the Prince of Jin, Rong, to finish the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yihai, the emperor attended the morning sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Dressed in full ceremonial regalia, he was helped up the steps by attendants on either side. He reached only one chamber, offered the libation, but was unable to complete the bow and had to withdraw. He then ordered Prince Rong of Jin to finish the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 是夕，宿南郊，疾尤劇，幾不救，夜分小愈。

translations.literal: That evening he lodged at the southern suburb. His illness grew especially severe, and he was nearly beyond saving, but after midnight he improved slightly.
translations.idiomatic: That night he stayed at the southern suburb. His illness worsened sharply and he nearly died, but after midnight he recovered a little.

sentences.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武皇帝中顯德元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Zhongxiande of Emperor Taizu, the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, and Martial (
translations.idiomatic: The first year of Zhongxiande of Emperor Taizu, the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, and Martial (

sentences.zh: 甲寅，公元九五四年）

translations.literal: on the day Jiayin, AD 954)
translations.idiomatic: on the day Jiayin, AD 954)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙子朔，帝祀圜丘，僅能瞻仰致敬而已，進爵奠幣皆有司代之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day Bingzi, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound. He was barely able to gaze upward and pay respects; the offering of wine and silks was all performed by officials in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, Bingzi, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound. He could do little more than look up and pay his respects, while officials performed the wine offerings and silk presentations on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was issued, and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 聽蜀境通商。

translations.literal: Trade through the Shu border was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Trade across the Shu frontier was permitted.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，罷鄴都，但為天雄軍。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, Ye was abolished as a capital and retained only as the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuyin, the Ye capital was abolished, and the city remained merely the seat of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，加晉王榮兼侍中，判內外兵馬事。

translations.literal: On the day Gengchen, the Prince of Jin, Rong, was additionally appointed concurrent Palace Secretary and put in charge of internal and external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengchen, Prince Rong of Jin was additionally made Palace Secretary and placed in charge of all military affairs, both within and beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 時群臣希得見帝，中外恐懼，聞晉王典兵，人心稍安。

translations.literal: At that time the ministers rarely saw the emperor, and both inside and outside the court were fearful. When they heard that the Prince of Jin held military command, people's hearts were somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the ministers seldom saw the emperor, and fear spread through the court and the realm. When word spread that Prince Rong of Jin had taken charge of the army, people began to feel somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 軍士有流言郊賞薄於唐明宗時者，帝聞之，壬午，召諸將至寢殿，讓之曰：「朕自即位以來，惡衣菲食，專以贍軍為念。

translations.literal: Among the soldiers there was a rumor that the rewards given at the suburban sacrifice were less generous than under Emperor Mingzong of Tang. When the emperor heard this, on the day Renwu he summoned the generals to his sleeping hall and rebuked them, saying, "Since I ascended the throne, I have worn poor clothes and eaten sparingly, devoting myself solely to supplying the army.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread among the soldiers that the rewards distributed at the suburban sacrifice were less generous than in the time of Tang Mingzong. When the emperor heard this, on the day Renwu he summoned the generals to his private hall and rebuked them, saying, "Since I took the throne, I have lived frugally and eaten simply, thinking only of providing for the army.

sentences.zh: 府庫蓄積，四方貢獻，贍軍之外，鮮有贏餘，汝輩豈不知之！

translations.literal: The treasury stores and tribute from all directions, beyond what is needed to supply the army, have scarcely any surplus. Do you not know this!
translations.idiomatic: Everything in the treasury and all tribute from the provinces goes to the army; there is almost nothing left over. Do you really not know this?

sentences.zh: 今乃縱兇徒騰口，不顧人主之勤儉，察國之貧乏，又不思己有何功而受賞，惟知怨望，於汝輩安乎！」

translations.literal: Now you let violent men wag their tongues, heedless of the sovereign's frugality and the state's poverty, without considering what merit you yourselves have to receive rewards, knowing only resentment—does this sit well with you!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you let malcontents spread rumors, with no regard for your ruler's thrift or the state's poverty, never asking what merit you have earned such rewards, and knowing only how to complain—is that acceptable to you?"

sentences.zh: 皆惶恐謝罪，退，索不逞者戮之，流言乃息。

translations.literal: All were fearful and apologized. After they withdrew, he sought out the unruly ones and executed them, and the rumors then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They all apologized in fear. After they left, he had the ringleaders hunted down and executed, and the rumors died away.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在鄴都，奇愛小吏曹翰之才，使之事晉王榮。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at Ye, he took special delight in the talent of the junior clerk Cao Han and had him serve the Prince of Jin, Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was at Ye, he had been greatly impressed by the ability of the junior clerk Cao Han and assigned him to serve Prince Rong of Jin.

sentences.zh: 榮鎮澶州，以為牙將。

translations.literal: When Rong governed Danzhou, he made Han a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was posted to Danzhou, he made Han one of his guard officers.

sentences.zh: 榮入為開封尹，未別召翰，翰自至，榮怪之。

translations.literal: When Rong entered the capital as intendant of Kaifeng, Han had not been separately summoned, yet he came on his own. Rong wondered at this.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong became intendant of Kaifeng, Han had not been specially summoned, yet he appeared on his own, which surprised Rong.

sentences.zh: 翰請間言曰：「大王，國之儲嗣，今主上寢疾，大王當入侍醫藥，奈何猶決事於外邪！」

translations.literal: Han requested a private audience and said, "Great Prince, you are the heir to the state. The sovereign is now bedridden with illness. You ought to attend at his bedside with medicine—why are you still conducting affairs outside the palace!"
translations.idiomatic: Han asked for a private word and said, "Your Highness is the heir to the throne. The emperor is now gravely ill in bed. You should be at his side tending to his care—why are you still handling affairs outside the palace?"

sentences.zh: 榮感悟，即日入止禁中。

translations.literal: Rong was moved by this and that same day entered and remained within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this advice, Rong entered the palace that very day and stayed there.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，帝疾篤，停諸司細務皆勿奏，有大事，則晉王榮稟進止宣行之。

translations.literal: On the day Bingxu, the emperor's illness became critical. All minor business from the various offices was halted and no longer submitted. For major affairs, the Prince of Jin, Rong, was to receive instructions and promulgate them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingxu, the emperor's condition grew critical. Routine business from all departments was suspended, and for major matters Prince Rong of Jin was to receive the emperor's decisions and carry them out.

sentences.zh: 以鎮寧節度使鄭仁誨為樞密使、同平章事。

translations.literal: Zheng Renhui, military governor of Zhenning, was appointed Privy Council commissioner and co–Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Renhui, military governor of Zhenning, was appointed Privy Council commissioner and co–Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以義武留後孫行友、保義留後韓通、朔方留後馮繼業皆為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day Wuzi, the acting governors Sun Xingyou of Yiwu, Han Tong of Baoyi, and Feng Jiye of Shuofang were all appointed full military governors.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuzi, Sun Xingyou of Yiwu, Han Tong of Baoyi, and Feng Jiye of Shuofang, who had been serving as acting governors, were all confirmed as military governors.

sentences.zh: 通，太原人也。

translations.literal: Tong was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tong was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝屢戒晉王曰：「昔吾西征，見唐十八陵無不發掘者，此無他，惟多藏金玉故也。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly admonished the Prince of Jin, saying, "On my western campaign I saw that none of the eighteen Tang tombs had escaped being plundered. This had no other cause than that they were filled with gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly warned Prince Rong of Jin, saying, "On my western campaign I saw that every one of the eighteen Tang imperial tombs had been looted. There is only one reason for that: they were stuffed with gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 我死，當衣以紙衣，斂以瓦棺；

translations.literal: When I die, dress me in paper garments and place me in an earthenware coffin;
translations.idiomatic: When I die, bury me in paper garments and an earthenware coffin;

sentences.zh: 速營葬，勿久留宮中；

translations.literal: bury me quickly and do not keep my body long in the palace;
translations.idiomatic: bury me quickly, and do not keep my body in the palace for long;

sentences.zh: 壙中無用石，以甓代之；

translations.literal: use no stone in the burial chamber, but brick instead;
translations.idiomatic: use no stone in the tomb chamber—use brick instead;

sentences.zh: 工人役徒皆和雇，勿以煩民；

translations.literal: hire all workers and laborers by contract, and do not trouble the people;
translations.idiomatic: hire all laborers at fair wages, and do not impose burdens on the people;

sentences.zh: 葬畢，募近陵民三十戶，蠲其雜徭，使之守視；

translations.literal: after the burial, recruit thirty households near the tomb, exempt them from miscellaneous corvée, and have them guard and watch over it;
translations.idiomatic: after the burial, recruit thirty households living near the tomb, exempt them from miscellaneous labor obligations, and have them guard it;

sentences.zh: 勿修下宮，勿置守陵宮人，勿作石羊、虎、人、馬，惟刻石置陵前云：『周天子平生好儉約，遺令用紙衣、瓦棺，嗣天子不敢違也。』

translations.literal: do not build an underground palace, do not place palace women to guard the tomb, do not make stone sheep, tigers, human figures, or horses—only carve a stone and place it before the tomb saying: 'The Son of Heaven of Zhou in life loved frugality. His testament orders paper garments and an earthenware coffin. The succeeding Son of Heaven dares not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: do not build an underground palace, do not station palace women to guard the tomb, and do not set up stone sheep, tigers, human figures, or horses. Only carve a stone tablet and place it before the tomb with these words: 'The Zhou emperor in life loved simplicity. His final command was for paper garments and an earthenware coffin. The succeeding emperor dares not disobey.

sentences.zh: 汝或吾違，吾不福汝！」

translations.literal: If you disobey me, I will not bless you!"
translations.idiomatic: If you disobey me, I will give you no blessing!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「李洪義當與節鉞，魏仁浦勿使離樞密院。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Li Hongyi should be granted a military commission, and Wei Renpu must not be removed from the Privy Council."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Li Hongyi should be given a military commission, and Wei Renpu must not be removed from the Privy Council."

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔前登州刺史周訓等塞決河。

translations.literal: On the day Gengyin, an edict ordered the former prefect of Dengzhou, Zhou Xun, and others to dam the breached river.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengyin, an edict ordered Zhou Xun, the former prefect of Dengzhou, and others to dam the breached sections of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 先是，河決靈河、魚池、酸棗、陽武、常樂驛、河陰、六明鎮、原武凡八口。

translations.literal: Earlier the river had breached at Linghe, Yuchi, Suanzao, Yangwu, Changle Post, Heyin, Liuming Town, and Yuanwu—eight breaches in all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the river had broken through at eight points: Linghe, Yuchi, Suanzao, Yangwu, Changle Post, Heyin, Liuming Town, and Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 至是分遣使者塞之。

translations.literal: At this point envoys were dispatched separately to block them.
translations.idiomatic: The court now sent out envoys to dam each breach separately.

sentences.zh: 帝命趣草制，以端明殿學士、戶部侍郎王溥為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered an edict drafted in haste appointing Wang Pu, academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue, as vice director of the Secretariat and co–Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an edict drafted urgently appointing Wang Pu, academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue, as vice director of the Secretariat and co–Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，宣制畢，左右以聞，帝曰：「吾無恨矣！」

translations.literal: On the day Renchen, after the edict had been promulgated, the attendants reported this to him. The emperor said, "I have no regrets!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renchen, after the edict had been announced, his attendants reported back to him. The emperor said, "I have no regrets!"

sentences.zh: 以樞密副使王仁鎬為永興節度使，以殿前都指揮使李重進領武信節度使，馬軍都指揮使樊愛能領武定節度使，步軍都指揮使何徽領昭武節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Rengu, vice commissioner of the Privy Council, was appointed military governor of Yongxing. Li Chongjin, commander of the Palace Front Army, was made acting military governor of Wuxin. Fan Aineng, commander of the cavalry, was made acting military governor of Wuding. He Hui, commander of the infantry, was made acting military governor of Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rengu, vice commissioner of the Privy Council, was appointed military governor of Yongxing. Li Chongjin, commander of the Palace Front Army, was made acting military governor of Wuxin; Fan Aineng, commander of the cavalry, acting military governor of Wuding; and He Hui, commander of the infantry, acting military governor of Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 重進年長於晉王榮，帝召入禁中，屬以後事，仍命拜榮，以定君臣之分。

translations.literal: Chongjin was older than the Prince of Jin, Rong. The emperor summoned him into the palace, entrusted him with affairs after his death, and still ordered him to bow to Rong in order to establish the distinction between ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin was older than Prince Rong of Jin. The emperor summoned him into the palace, entrusted him with affairs after his death, and nevertheless ordered him to bow to Rong so as to fix the proper relation between sovereign and subject.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝殂於滋德殿，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: That same day the emperor died in Zide Hall. The death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor died in Zide Hall. His death was kept secret and no mourning was publicly announced.

sentences.zh: 乙未，宣遺制。

translations.literal: On the day Yiwei, the testament was announced.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiwei, the emperor's final testament was announced.

sentences.zh: 丙申，晉王即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On the day Bingchen, the Prince of Jin ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingchen, Prince Rong of Jin ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，靜海節度使吳權卒，子昌岌立。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu Quan, military governor of Jinghai, had died, and his son Changji succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wu Quan, military governor of Jinghai, had died, and his son Changji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 昌岌卒，弟昌文立。

translations.literal: Changji died, and his younger brother Changwen succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Changji died, his younger brother Changwen took his place.

sentences.zh: 是月，始請命於南漢，南漢以昌文為靜海節度使兼安南都護。

translations.literal: That month he first requested appointment from Southern Han, and Southern Han appointed Changwen military governor of Jinghai and concurrently Protector-General of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: That month he first sought formal recognition from Southern Han, which appointed Changwen military governor of Jinghai and concurrently Protector-General of Annam.

sentences.zh: 北漢主聞太祖晏駕，甚喜，謀大舉入寇，遣使請兵於契丹。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han heard that Emperor Taizu had died and was greatly pleased. He plotted a major invasion and sent an envoy to request troops from the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler of Northern Han learned that Emperor Taizu had died, he was delighted and planned a major invasion, sending an envoy to ask the Khitan for troops.

sentences.zh: 二月，契丹遣其武定節度使、政事令楊兗將萬餘騎如晉陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Khitan sent their Wuding military governor and director of political affairs, Yang Wan, leading more than ten thousand cavalry toward Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Khitan sent Yang Wan, their military governor of Wuding and director of political affairs, with more than ten thousand cavalry toward Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 北漢主自將兵三萬，以義成節度使白從暉為行軍都部署，武寧節度使張元徽為前鋒都指揮使，與契丹自團柏南趣潞州。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han personally led thirty thousand troops, with Bai Conghui, military governor of Yicheng, as overall campaign commander and Zhang Yuanhui, military governor of Wuning, as vanguard commander. Together with the Khitan they advanced south from Tuanbai toward Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Northern Han personally led thirty thousand troops, appointing Bai Conghui, military governor of Yicheng, as overall campaign commander and Zhang Yuanhui, military governor of Wuning, as vanguard commander. Together with the Khitan, they marched south from Tuanbai toward Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀左匡聖馬步都指揮使、保寧節度使安思謙譖殺張業，廢趙廷隱，蜀人皆惡之。

translations.literal: An Siqian of Shu, Left Kuangsheng commander of cavalry and infantry and military governor of Baoning, slandered and killed Zhang Ye and deposed Zhao Tingyin. All the people of Shu detested him.
translations.idiomatic: An Siqian of Shu, commander of cavalry and infantry under the Left Kuangsheng banner and military governor of Baoning, had Zhang Ye killed on false charges and Zhao Tingyin removed from office, and the people of Shu universally despised him.

sentences.zh: 蜀主使將兵救王景崇，思謙逗橈無功，內慚懼，不自安。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler sent him to lead troops to rescue Wang Jingchong. Siqian dithered and achieved nothing. Inwardly ashamed and fearful, he could not feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler sent him to lead troops to relieve Wang Jingchong, but Siqian dragged his feet and accomplished nothing. Ashamed and afraid, he grew increasingly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 自張業之誅，宮門守衛加嚴，思謙以為疑己，言多不遜。

translations.literal: Since Zhang Ye's execution, security at the palace gates had been tightened. Siqian believed himself suspected and his words were often insolent.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Ye's execution, security at the palace gates was tightened. Siqian took this as a sign that he was under suspicion, and his speech grew increasingly insolent.

sentences.zh: 思謙典宿衛，多殺士卒以立威。

translations.literal: Siqian commanded the night guard and often killed soldiers to establish his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Siqian commanded the palace night guard and frequently killed soldiers to assert his authority.

sentences.zh: 蜀主閱衛士，有年尚壯而為思謙所斥者，復留隸籍，思謙殺之，蜀主不能平。

translations.literal: When the Shu ruler reviewed the guards, some who were still vigorous but had been dismissed by Siqian were kept on the rolls. Siqian killed them, and the Shu ruler could not reconcile himself to this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu ruler inspected the palace guards, he found men who were still fit for service but had been dismissed by Siqian yet kept on the rolls. Siqian had them killed, and the Shu ruler could not accept it.

sentences.zh: 思謙三子，扆、嗣、裔，倚父勢暴橫，為國人患。

translations.literal: Siqian's three sons—Yi, Si, and Yi—relied on their father's power to act violently and arrogantly, and were a scourge to the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Siqian's three sons—Yi, Si, and Yi—used their father's power to terrorize others and became a plague on the realm.

sentences.zh: 翰林使王藻屢言思謙怨望，將反，丁巳，思謙入朝，蜀主命壯士擊殺之，及其三子。

translations.literal: Wang Zao, a Hanlin envoy, repeatedly said that Siqian harbored resentment and would rebel. On the day Dingsi, Siqian entered court, and the Shu ruler ordered strongmen to strike and kill him along with his three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao, a Hanlin envoy, repeatedly reported that Siqian was discontent and plotting rebellion. On the day Dingsi, when Siqian came to court, the Shu ruler ordered armed men to strike him down, together with his three sons.

sentences.zh: 藻亦坐擅啟邊奏，並誅之。

translations.literal: Zao was also punished for unauthorized opening of border reports, and was executed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was also executed, charged with having improperly opened frontier dispatches.

sentences.zh: 北漢兵屯梁侯驛，昭義節度使李筠遣其將穆令均將步騎二千逆戰，筠自將大軍壁於太平驛。

translations.literal: The Northern Han army encamped at Lianghou Post. Li Jun, military governor of Zhaoyi, sent his general Mu Lingjun with two thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose them, while Jun himself led the main army and fortified at Taiping Post.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Han army encamped at Lianghou Post. Li Jun, military governor of Zhaoyi, sent his general Mu Lingjun with two thousand infantry and cavalry to meet them, while he himself led the main force and fortified at Taiping Post.

sentences.zh: 張元徽與令均戰，陽不勝而北，令均逐之，伏發，殺令均，俘斬士卒千餘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanhui fought Lingjun, feigned defeat, and retreated north. Lingjun pursued him, but an ambush was sprung. Lingjun was killed, and more than a thousand soldiers were captured or slain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanhui engaged Lingjun, pretended to be beaten, and withdrew to the north. Lingjun pursued him into an ambush, was killed, and more than a thousand of his men were captured or slain.

sentences.zh: 筠遁歸上黨，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Jun fled back to Shangdang and held the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun fled back to Shangdang and shut himself up in the city to defend it.

sentences.zh: 筠，即李榮也，避上名改焉。

translations.literal: Jun was in fact Li Rong, who had changed his name to avoid the taboo of the new emperor's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun was originally named Li Rong; he had changed his name to avoid the taboo on the new emperor's personal name.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞北漢主入寇，欲自將兵御之，群臣皆曰：「劉崇自平陽遁走以來，勢蹙氣沮，必不敢自來。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong heard that the ruler of Northern Han had invaded and wished to lead the army himself to repel him. All the ministers said, "Since Liu Chong fled from Pingyang, his momentum has been constricted and his spirits dampened. He will surely not dare come in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong heard that the ruler of Northern Han had invaded, he wanted to lead the army himself to repel the attack. His ministers all said, "Since Liu Chong fled from Pingyang, his strength has been broken and his morale shattered. He will surely not dare come in person.

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 山陵有日，人心易搖，不宜輕動，宜命將御之。」

translations.literal: The imperial burial is imminent, and people's hearts are easily unsettled. It is not fitting to move lightly. You should appoint generals to repel the invaders."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial burial is near at hand, and the people's loyalty is easily shaken. You should not take the field yourself. It would be better to appoint generals to meet the invasion."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「崇幸我大喪，輕朕年少新立，有吞天下之心，此必自來，朕不可不往。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Chong has taken advantage of our great mourning, underestimates me as young and newly enthroned, and harbors the ambition to swallow the empire. He will surely come in person himself. I cannot fail to go."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "Liu Chong has seized on our period of mourning, thinks little of me because I am young and have only just ascended the throne, and means to swallow the realm. He will surely come himself—and I cannot stay away."

sentences.zh: 馮道固爭之，帝曰：「昔唐太宗定天下，未嘗不自行，朕何敢偷安！」

translations.literal: Feng Dao firmly remonstrated with him. The Emperor said, "In the past, when Emperor Taizong of Tang settled the empire, he never failed to go in person. How dare I seek ease for myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao pressed his objection hard, but the Emperor said, "When Emperor Taizong of Tang brought the empire under his rule, he always took the field himself. How can I shrink from doing the same?"

sentences.zh: 道曰：「未審陛下能為唐太宗否？」

translations.literal: Dao said, "It is not yet clear whether Your Majesty can be like Emperor Taizong of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao asked, "Are you certain that you can be another Emperor Taizong of Tang?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「以吾兵力之強，破劉崇如山壓卵耳！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "With the strength of our military power, breaking Liu Chong will be like a mountain crushing an egg!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered, "With the army I have, crushing Liu Chong will be like a mountain falling on an egg!"

sentences.zh: 道曰：「未審陛下能為山否？」

translations.literal: Dao said, "It is not yet clear whether Your Majesty can be the mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao replied dryly, "Are you certain that you can be the mountain?"

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 惟王溥勸行，帝從之。

translations.literal: Only Wang Pu urged him to go, and the Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Pu urged the campaign, and the Emperor took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙亥朔，蜀主加捧聖、控鶴都指揮使兼中書令孫漢韶武信節度使，賜爵樂安郡王，罷軍職。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day of the yihai new moon, the ruler of Shu promoted Sun Hanshao—Commander of the Pangsheng and Konghe Guards and concurrently Grand Councilor—to Military Governor of Wuxin, enfeoffed him as Prince of Lean Commandery, and removed him from his military posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of the cycle (yihai), the Shu ruler made Sun Hanshao, commander of the Pangsheng and Konghe guards and concurrent grand councilor, military governor of Wuxin, created him Prince of Lean Commandery, and relieved him of his army commands.

sentences.zh: 蜀主懲安思謙之跋扈，命山南西道節度使李廷珪等十人分典禁兵。

translations.literal: The ruler of Shu, chastened by An Siqian's overbearing conduct, ordered Li Tinggui, Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit, and nine others to divide command of the palace troops among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Having been burned by An Siqian's arrogance, the Shu ruler ordered Li Tinggui, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, and nine other men to share command of the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 北漢乘勝進逼潞州。

translations.literal: Northern Han pressed its advantage and advanced against Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han pressed its victory and pushed on toward Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，詔天雄節度使符彥卿引兵自磁州固鎮出北漢軍後，以鎮寧節度使郭崇副之；

translations.literal: On dingchou, an edict commanded Fu Yanqing, Military Governor of Tianxiong, to lead troops from Guzhen in Cizhou to emerge behind the Northern Han army, with Guo Chong, Military Governor of Zhenning, as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the court ordered Fu Yanqing, military governor of Tianxiong, to march from Guzhen in Cizhou and fall on the rear of the Northern Han army, with Guo Chong, military governor of Zhenning, as his second-in-command;

sentences.zh: 又詔河中節度使王彥超引兵自晉州東出邀北漢軍，以保義節度使韓通副之；

translations.literal: It further commanded Wang Yanchao, Military Governor of Hezhong, to lead troops east from Jinzhou to intercept the Northern Han army, with Han Tong, Military Governor of Baoyi, as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: it also ordered Wang Yanchao, military governor of Hezhong, to move east from Jinzhou and block the Northern Han army, with Han Tong, military governor of Baoyi, supporting him;

sentences.zh: 又命馬軍都指揮使、寧江節度使樊愛能、步軍都指揮使、清淮節度使何徽、義成節度使白重贊、鄭州防禦使史彥超、前耀州團練使符彥能將兵先趣澤州，宣微使向訓監之。

translations.literal: It further ordered Fan Aineng—Commander of the Horse Army and Military Governor of Ningjiang—He Hui—Commander of the Foot Army and Military Governor of Qinghuai—Bai Chongzan, Military Governor of Yicheng—Shi Yanchao, Defender of Zhengzhou—and Fu Yanneng, former regimental trainer of Yaozhou—to lead troops first to Zezhou, with Xuanwei Commissioner Xiang Xun supervising them.
translations.idiomatic: and it sent Fan Aineng, commander of the horse army and military governor of Ningjiang; He Hui, commander of the foot army and military governor of Qinghuai; Bai Chongzan, military governor of Yicheng; Shi Yanchao, defender of Zhengzhou; and Fu Yanneng, former regimental trainer of Yaozhou, ahead to Zezhou under the supervision of palace commissioner Xiang Xun.

sentences.zh: 重贊，憲州人也。

translations.literal: Chongzan was a native of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Chongzan was a native of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸未，帝命馮道奉梓宮赴山陵，以鄭仁誨為東京留守。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Emperor ordered Feng Dao to escort the coffin to the imperial tomb and appointed Zheng Renhui as regent of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the Emperor sent Feng Dao to escort the late emperor's coffin to the burial mound and appointed Zheng Renhui to remain behind as regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Emperor departed from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the Emperor set out from Daliang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，至懷州。

translations.literal: On gengyin, he reached Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he reached Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝欲兼行速進，控鶴都指揮使真定趙晁私謂通事舍人鄭好謙曰：「賊勢方盛，宜持重以挫之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to advance rapidly by forced marches. Zhao Chao of Zhending, Commander of the Konghe Guards, privately said to Palace Attendant Zheng Haoqian, "The enemy's momentum is at its height. We should proceed with caution to wear them down."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted to press forward at forced-march speed, but Zhao Chao of Zhending, commander of the Konghe guards, told palace attendant Zheng Haoqian in private, "The enemy is at the height of its strength. We should move deliberately and break their momentum."

sentences.zh: 好謙言於帝，帝怒曰：「汝安得此言！

translations.literal: Haoqian reported this to the Emperor. The Emperor angrily said, "How dare you speak such words!
translations.idiomatic: Haoqian repeated this to the Emperor, who flew into a rage. "How dare you say such a thing!

sentences.zh: 必為人所使，言其人則生，不然必死，」好謙以實對，帝命並晁械於州獄。

translations.literal: You must have been put up to this by someone. Name that person and you shall live; otherwise you shall surely die." Haoqian answered truthfully, and the Emperor ordered both him and Chao shackled in the prison of the prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Someone must have put you up to this. Name him and you live; refuse and you die." Haoqian told the truth, and the Emperor had both men clapped in irons in the local jail."

sentences.zh: 壬辰，帝過澤州，宿於州東北。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Emperor passed through Zezhou and lodged northeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Emperor passed through Zezhou and camped northeast of the city.

sentences.zh: 北漢主不知帝至，過潞州不攻，引兵而南，是夕，軍於高平之南。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han did not know the Emperor had arrived. He passed Luzhou without attacking, led his army southward, and that evening encamped south of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong did not yet know the Zhou emperor had arrived. He bypassed Luzhou without assaulting it, marched south, and that night encamped south of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，前鋒與北漢兵遇，擊之，北漢兵卻。

translations.literal: On guisi, the vanguard encountered Northern Han troops, attacked them, and the Northern Han army retreated.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the vanguard met the Northern Han army, struck them, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 帝慮其遁去，趣諸軍亟進。

translations.literal: The Emperor, fearing they would escape, urged all the armies to advance swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the enemy would slip away, the Emperor ordered every unit forward at once.

sentences.zh: 北漢主以中軍陳於巴公原，張元徽軍其東，楊兗軍其西，眾頗嚴整。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han deployed his central army on Bagong Plain, with Zhang Yuanhui's force on the east and Yang Gun's on the west. The formation was quite orderly and tight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong drew up his main force on Bagong Plain, with Zhang Yuanhui on the east and Yang Gun on the west. The array was tight and imposing.

sentences.zh: 時河陽節度使劉詞將後軍未至，眾心危懼，而帝志氣益銳，命白重贊與侍衛馬步都虞候李重進將左軍居西，樊愛能、何徽將右軍居東，向訓、史彥超將精騎居中央，殿前都指揮使張永德將禁兵衛帝。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Ci, Military Governor of Heyang, had not yet arrived with the rear army, and the troops' hearts were fearful and apprehensive. Yet the Emperor's spirit grew only sharper. He ordered Bai Chongzan and Li Chongjin, Chief Adjutant of the Palace Horse and Foot Guards, to command the left army on the west; Fan Aineng and He Hui to command the right army on the east; Xiang Xun and Shi Yanchao to lead elite cavalry in the center; and Zhang Yongde, Commander of the Palace Front Army, to lead the palace troops to guard the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ci, military governor of Heyang, had not yet come up with the rear guard, and morale wavered—but the Emperor's resolve only hardened. He placed Bai Chongzan and palace adjutant Li Chongjin on the left in the west, Fan Aineng and He Hui on the right in the east, Xiang Xun and Shi Yanchao with picked cavalry in the center, and Zhang Yongde with the palace guard around himself.

sentences.zh: 帝介馬自臨陳督戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor, armored and mounted, personally came to the battle line to direct the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Armored and on horseback, the Emperor rode to the front to command the battle in person.

sentences.zh: 北漢主見周軍少，悔召契丹，謂諸將曰：「吾自用漢軍可破也，何必契丹！

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han saw that the Zhou army was few in number, regretted having summoned the Khitan, and said to his generals, "I can break them using Han troops alone—why need the Khitan!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how small the Zhou force was, Liu Chong regretted calling in the Khitan and told his generals, "My own Han troops are enough to crush them—what need have I of the Khitan!

sentences.zh: 今日不惟克周，亦可使契丹心服。」

translations.literal: Today we will not only defeat Zhou, but also make the Khitan submit in their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: If we win today, we will not only defeat Zhou—we will make the Khitan respect us as well."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆以為然。

translations.literal: All the generals agreed that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all agreed.

sentences.zh: 楊兗策馬前望周軍，退謂北漢主曰：「勍敵也，未可輕進！」

translations.literal: Yang Gun spurred his horse forward to observe the Zhou army, then withdrew and said to the ruler of Northern Han, "They are formidable foes. We must not advance lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun rode forward for a closer look at the Zhou lines, then came back and warned Liu Chong, "These are tough enemies. We must not rush in!"

sentences.zh: 北漢主奮髯，曰：「時不可失，請公勿言，試觀我戰。」

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han bristled his beard and said, "The moment must not be lost. I beg you say no more—watch how I fight."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong's beard bristled with impatience. "The moment won't wait," he said. "Say no more—watch me fight."

sentences.zh: 兗默然不悅。

translations.literal: Gun fell silent, displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun said nothing, plainly unhappy.

sentences.zh: 時東北風方盛，俄而忽轉南風，北漢副樞密使王延嗣使司天監李義白北漢主云：「時可戰矣。」

translations.literal: At that time a strong northeast wind was blowing, but suddenly it shifted to a south wind. Wang Yansi, Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs of Northern Han, had Li Yi of the Directorate of Astronomy report to the ruler of Northern Han, "The time to fight has come."
translations.idiomatic: A strong northeast wind was blowing when, suddenly, it swung round to the south. Wang Yansi, Northern Han's deputy commissioner of military affairs, had the court astronomer Li Yi tell Liu Chong, "The moment to fight has come."

sentences.zh: 北漢主從之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong accepted the omen.

sentences.zh: 樞密直學士王得中扣馬諫曰：「義可斬也！

translations.literal: Wang Dezhong, Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, seized the bridle of the ruler's horse and remonstrated, "Yi deserves to be executed!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dezhong, an academician of the bureau of military affairs, grabbed the bridle of Liu Chong's horse and protested, "Li Yi deserves death!

sentences.zh: 風勢如此，豈助我者邪！」

translations.literal: With the wind in this condition, how can it be helping us!"
translations.idiomatic: A wind like this helps the enemy, not us!"

sentences.zh: 北漢主曰：「吾計已決，老書生勿妄言，且斬汝！」

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han said, "My plan is already settled. Old bookworm, do not speak rashly—or I shall cut you down first!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong snapped, "My mind is made up. Hold your tongue, old pedant, or I'll cut you down myself!"

sentences.zh: 麾東軍先進，張元徽將千騎擊周右軍。

translations.literal: He waved the eastern army forward first, and Zhang Yuanhui led a thousand horsemen to strike the Zhou right wing.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the eastern wing forward, and Zhang Yuanhui led a thousand horsemen against the Zhou right.

sentences.zh: 合戰未幾，樊愛能、何徽引騎兵先遁，右軍潰。

translations.literal: After the armies had joined battle only briefly, Fan Aineng and He Hui led the cavalry in flight first, and the right wing collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the battle begun when Fan Aineng and He Hui bolted with their cavalry, and the right wing broke apart.

sentences.zh: 步兵千餘人解甲呼萬歲，降於北漢。

translations.literal: More than a thousand foot soldiers doffed their armor, shouted "Long live the Emperor!" and surrendered to Northern Han.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand foot soldiers threw off their armor, shouted "Long live the emperor!" and went over to Northern Han.

sentences.zh: 帝見軍勢危，自引親兵犯矢石督戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw that the army's situation was perilous and personally led his personal troops through flying arrows and stones to direct the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the battle turn against him, the Emperor himself led his personal guard through a hail of arrows and stones to rally the line.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝時為宿衛將，謂同列曰：「主危如此，吾屬何得不致死！」

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taizu was serving as a palace guard commander. He said to his comrades, "Our lord is in such danger—how can we fail to fight to the death!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Emperor Taizu, Zhao Kuangyin, was a palace guard commander. He told his fellows, "The emperor is in peril—how can we hold back our lives now!"

sentences.zh: 又謂張永德曰：「賊氣驕，力戰可破也！

translations.literal: He further said to Zhang Yongde, "The enemy's spirit is arrogant. If we fight hard, they can be broken!
translations.idiomatic: Then he said to Zhang Yongde, "The enemy is overconfident. Hit them hard and they'll break!

sentences.zh: 公麾下多能左射者，請引兵乘高西出為左翼，我引兵為右翼以擊之。

translations.literal: Many under your command can shoot from the left. Please lead troops over high ground to the west as the left wing; I shall lead troops as the right wing to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of your men can shoot from the left side of the saddle. Take the high ground to the west as our left wing; I'll take the right and we'll hit them together.

sentences.zh: 國家安危，在此一舉！」

translations.literal: The safety or peril of the state hangs on this one stroke!"
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the dynasty rests on this one charge!"

sentences.zh: 永德從之，各將二千人進戰。

translations.literal: Yongde followed his plan, and each led two thousand men forward into battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde agreed, and each man led two thousand troops into the fight.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝身先士卒，馳犯其鋒，士卒死戰，無不一當百，北漢兵披靡。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu took the lead before the soldiers, charged into the enemy's front, and his troops fought to the death—each man counted as a hundred—and the Northern Han army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu himself led the charge straight into the enemy van. His men fought as though each one were worth a hundred, and the Northern Han line crumbled.

sentences.zh: 內殿直夏津馬仁瑀謂眾曰：「使乘輿受敵，安用我輩！」

translations.literal: Ma Renyu of Xiajin, an Inner Palace Guard, said to the troops, "If we let the imperial carriage take the enemy's blows, what use are we!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Renyu of Xiajin, of the inner palace guard, shouted to the men around him, "If the emperor himself must face the enemy, what are we here for!"

sentences.zh: 躍馬引弓大呼，連斃數十人，士氣益振。

translations.literal: He leapt on his horse, drew his bow, and shouted loudly, killing several tens of men in succession, and the troops' morale surged all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred forward, loosed arrow after arrow with a great shout, and cut down dozens of men in succession. The army's spirit soared.

sentences.zh: 殿前右番行首馬全乂言於帝曰：「賊勢極矣，將為我擒，願陛下按轡勿動，徐觀諸將破之。」

translations.literal: Ma Quanyi, chief of the right rotation in the Palace Front Army, said to the Emperor, "The enemy's momentum is exhausted. They are about to be captured by us. I beg Your Majesty to hold the reins and not move, and watch calmly as the generals break them."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanyi, chief of the right rotation of the palace front guard, told the Emperor, "The enemy is spent—they're as good as ours. Stay your horse, Your Majesty, and watch your generals finish them."

sentences.zh: 即引數百騎進陷陳。

translations.literal: He immediately led several hundred horsemen forward and broke into the enemy formation.
translations.idiomatic: Then he led several hundred horsemen straight into the enemy formation.

sentences.zh: 北漢主知帝自臨陳，褒賞張元徽，趣使乘勝進兵。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han learned that the Emperor was personally on the battle line. He praised and rewarded Zhang Yuanhui and urged him to press the advantage and advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong realized the Zhou emperor was fighting in person, he praised Zhang Yuanhui and ordered him to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 元徽前略陳，馬倒，為周兵所殺。

translations.literal: Yuanhui advanced to overrun the formation, his horse fell, and he was killed by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhui rode ahead to overrun the Zhou line, but his horse went down and Zhou soldiers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 元徽，北漢之驍將也，北軍由是奪氣。

translations.literal: Yuanhui was a fierce general of Northern Han, and from this the Northern army lost its fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhui had been Northern Han's fiercest fighter, and with his death the northern army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 時南風益盛，周兵爭奮，北漢兵大敗，北漢主自舉赤幟以收兵，不能止。

translations.literal: At that time the south wind blew all the stronger. The Zhou troops strove forward with redoubled ardor, and the Northern Han army was utterly defeated. The ruler of Northern Han himself raised red banners to rally the troops, but could not stop the rout.
translations.idiomatic: The south wind blew harder still. The Zhou soldiers fought with fresh fury, and Northern Han collapsed. Liu Chong himself raised red banners to recall his men, but nothing could stop the rout.

sentences.zh: 楊兗畏周兵之強，不敢救，且恨北漢主之語，全軍而退。

translations.literal: Yang Gun feared the strength of the Zhou army, dared not go to the rescue, and moreover resented the ruler of Northern Han's words. He withdrew with his entire army.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun, still smarting at Liu Chong's earlier rebuke and fearing the Zhou strength, refused to intervene and marched his whole force away.

sentences.zh: 樊愛能、何徽引數千騎南走，控弦露刃，剽掠輜重，役徒驚走，失亡甚多。

translations.literal: Fan Aineng and He Hui led several thousand horsemen south in flight, bows drawn and blades bared, plundering the baggage train. Laborers fled in panic, and losses were very great.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Aineng and He Hui fled south with several thousand horsemen, bows strung and swords naked, looting the supply train as they went. Camp followers scattered in terror, and the losses were enormous.

sentences.zh: 帝遣近臣及親軍校追諭止之，莫肯奉詔，使者或為軍士所殺，揚言：「契丹大至，官軍敗績，餘眾已降虜矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent close attendants and personal military officers to pursue them and order them to halt, but none would obey the edict. Some messengers were killed by the soldiers, who spread the word, "The Khitan have arrived in force. The government army has been defeated, and the survivors have already surrendered to the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent courtiers and trusted officers after them to bring them back, but none would obey. Some envoys were killed, and the fugitives spread the rumor, "The Khitan are upon us! The army is beaten and the rest have already gone over to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 劉詞遇愛能等於塗，愛能等止之，詞不從，引兵而北。

translations.literal: Liu Ci encountered Aineng and the others on the road. Aineng and the others tried to stop him, but Ci would not listen and led his troops northward.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Liu Ci met Fan Aineng and the others, who tried to turn him back, but he refused and pressed north with his troops.

sentences.zh: 時北漢主尚有餘眾萬餘人，阻澗而陳，薄暮，詞至，復與諸軍擊之，北漢兵又敗，殺王延嗣，追至高平，殭屍滿山谷，委棄御特及輜重、器械、雜畜不可勝紀。

translations.literal: At that time the ruler of Northern Han still had more than ten thousand remaining troops, who blocked a stream and formed battle lines. At dusk Ci arrived, joined the other armies in attacking them again, and the Northern Han army was defeated once more. Wang Yansi was killed. The pursuit reached Gaoping; corpses filled the valleys and hills, and abandoned imperial horses, baggage, weapons, and miscellaneous livestock were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong still had more than ten thousand men left, drawn up with a stream at their backs. At dusk Liu Ci came up, joined the other Zhou forces, and broke them again. Wang Yansi was killed. The pursuit rolled on to Gaoping; dead filled every valley, and abandoned horses, wagons, arms, and livestock lay strewn beyond count.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝宿於野次，得步兵之降敵者，皆殺之。

translations.literal: That evening the Emperor lodged in an open camp. Foot soldiers who had surrendered to the enemy were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Emperor camped in the open field and had every foot soldier who had gone over to the enemy executed.

sentences.zh: 樊愛能等聞周兵大捷，與士卒稍稍復還，有達曙不至者。

translations.literal: When Fan Aineng and the others heard of the Zhou army's great victory, they and their soldiers gradually returned, though some did not arrive until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Aineng and the rest heard of the great victory, they and their men drifted back by degrees—some not until dawn.

sentences.zh: 甲午，休兵於高平，選北漢降卒數千人為效順指揮，命前武勝行軍司馬唐景思將之，使戍淮上，餘二千餘人賜資裝縱遣之。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the army rested at Gaoping. Several thousand surrendered Northern Han soldiers were selected to form the Submission-Obedience Command. Tang Jingsi, former marching chief of staff of Wusheng, was ordered to lead them and garrison them on the Huai River frontier. The remaining more than two thousand were given travel funds and released.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the army rested at Gaoping. Several thousand Northern Han prisoners were formed into a Loyal Submission command under Tang Jingsi, former chief of staff of the Wusheng expedition, and sent to garrison the Huai frontier. The remaining two thousand-odd were given supplies and sent home.

sentences.zh: 李穀為亂兵所迫，潛竄山谷，數日乃出。

translations.literal: Li Gu was driven by the disorderly troops, hid himself in the mountains and valleys, and did not emerge until several days later.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu was caught up in the rout, hid in the hills for days, and only then made his way out.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，帝至潞州。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Emperor reached Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the Emperor reached Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 北漢主自高平被褐戴笠，乘契丹所贈黃騮，帥百餘騎由雕窠嶺遁歸，宵迷，俘村民為導，誤之晉州，行百餘里，乃覺之，殺導者。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han fled from Gaoping wearing coarse cloth and a bamboo hat, riding a yellow piebald horse given him by the Khitan, and led a little more than a hundred horsemen over Diaoke Ridge to escape homeward. He lost his way at night, seized villagers as guides, was misdirected toward Jinzhou, and after traveling more than a hundred li realized the error and killed the guides.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong slipped away from Gaoping in coarse dress and a bamboo hat, mounted on a yellow piebald the Khitan had given him, and led a little over a hundred horsemen over Diaoke Ridge. He lost his way in the dark, forced villagers to guide him, was led a hundred li toward Jinzhou before he realized the mistake, and killed the guides.

sentences.zh: 晝夜北走，所至，得食未舉箸，或傳周兵至，輒蒼黃而去。

translations.literal: Day and night he fled north. Wherever he stopped, if he had obtained food and not yet raised his chopsticks, or if word came that Zhou troops were approaching, he would flee in panic.
translations.idiomatic: He fled north day and night. Wherever he stopped, if food was set before him he would not even lift his chopsticks before word of Zhou pursuers sent him scrambling off again.

sentences.zh: 北漢主衰老力憊，仗於馬上，晝夜馳驟，殆不能支，僅得入晉陽。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han was aged and exhausted in strength. Leaning on his horse, he galloped day and night, barely able to hold on, and only just managed to enter Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Old and spent, Liu Chong rode slumped in the saddle, galloping without rest until he could scarcely go on, and only barely reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝欲誅樊愛能等以肅軍政，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to execute Fan Aineng and the others to restore military discipline, but hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted to execute Fan Aineng and the others to restore discipline, but hesitated.

sentences.zh: 己亥，晝臥行宮帳中，張永德侍側，帝以其事訪之，對曰「愛能等素無大功，忝冒節鉞，望敵先逃，死未塞責。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Emperor lay down to rest by day in the tent of the traveling palace. Zhang Yongde attended at his side. The Emperor consulted him on the matter, and he replied, "Aineng and the others have never had great achievements, yet shamefully hold command seals and battle-axes. They fled at sight of the enemy. Death would not exhaust their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Emperor was resting by day in his field tent with Zhang Yongde in attendance. When the Emperor asked his view, Yongde answered, "Fan Aineng and the rest have never earned their rank. They hold commander's seals they don't deserve, and they ran at the first sight of the enemy. Death is less than they owe.

sentences.zh: 且陛下方欲削平四海，苟軍法不立，雖有熊羆之士，百萬之眾，安得而用之！」

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty is just setting out to pacify the four seas. If military law is not established, even with warriors fierce as bears and tigers and an army of a million, how could you employ them!"
translations.idiomatic: And you mean to bring the realm under one rule. If military law counts for nothing, what good are a million men, however brave?"

sentences.zh: 帝擲枕於地，大呼稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor threw his pillow to the ground and cried out in approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hurled his pillow to the floor and shouted his approval.

sentences.zh: 即收愛能、徽及所部軍使以上七十餘人。

translations.literal: He immediately arrested Aineng, Hui, and more than seventy army officers of regimental commander rank and above under their command.
translations.idiomatic: He at once arrested Fan Aineng, He Hui, and more than seventy officers of regimental rank and above who served under them.

sentences.zh: 責之曰：「汝曹皆累朝宿將，非不能戰。

translations.literal: He rebuked them, saying, "You are all veteran generals of successive reigns. It is not that you cannot fight.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked them: "You are seasoned generals of several reigns. You know how to fight.

sentences.zh: 今望風奔遁者，無他，正欲以朕為奇貨，賣與劉崇耳！」

translations.literal: Those who now flee at sight of the wind have no other motive—they simply wish to treat me as a rare prize and sell me to Liu Chong!"
translations.idiomatic: You ran because you meant to hand me over to Liu Chong like a prize on the market!"

sentences.zh: 悉斬之。

translations.literal: All were executed.
translations.idiomatic: All were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 帝以何徽先守晉州有功，欲免之，既而以法不可廢，遂並誅之，而給槥歸葬。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because He Hui had earlier held Jinzhou with merit, wished to spare him, but then considered that the law could not be set aside, and so executed him as well, yet provided coffins for burial back home.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had wanted to spare He Hui for his earlier defense of Jinzhou, but decided the law could not bend and had him executed too—though he sent coffins so the men could be buried at home.

sentences.zh: 自是驕將惰卒始知所懼，不行姑息之政矣。

translations.literal: From this time forward, arrogant generals and lazy soldiers first learned what there was to fear, and the policy of undue leniency was no longer practiced.
translations.idiomatic: After that, arrogant commanders and slack soldiers learned to fear the consequences, and indulgence in the ranks came to an end.

sentences.zh: 庚子，賞高平之功，以李重進兼忠武節度使，向訓兼義成節度使，張永德兼武信節度使，史彥超為鎮國節度使。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the achievements at Gaoping were rewarded. Li Chongjin was made concurrent Military Governor of Zhongwu, Xiang Xun concurrent Military Governor of Yicheng, Zhang Yongde concurrent Military Governor of Wuxin, and Shi Yanchao Military Governor of Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the victors of Gaoping were rewarded: Li Chongjin was made concurrent military governor of Zhongwu, Xiang Xun of Yicheng, Zhang Yongde of Wuxin, and Shi Yanchao military governor of Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 張永德盛稱太祖皇帝之智勇，帝擢太祖皇帝為殿前都虞候，領嚴州刺史，以馬仁瑀為控鶴弓箭直指揮使，馬全乂為散員指揮使。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde spoke at length in praise of Emperor Taizu's wisdom and courage. The Emperor promoted Emperor Taizu to Chief Adjutant of the Palace Front Army and made him prefect of Yanzhou. Ma Renyu was made Commander of the Konghe Archers Direct Guard, and Ma Quanyi Commander of the Miscellaneous Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde praised Taizu's courage and judgment at length. The Emperor promoted him to chief adjutant of the palace front army and prefect of Yanzhou, made Ma Renyu commander of the Konghe archers guard, and Ma Quanyi commander of the miscellaneous guards.

sentences.zh: 自餘將校遷拜者凡數十人，士卒有自行間擢主軍廂者。

translations.literal: Several tens of other officers and commanders were promoted and enfeoffed, and among the soldiers some were raised from the ranks to command army companies.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen other officers were promoted as well, and some common soldiers were raised from the ranks to command companies.

sentences.zh: 釋趙晁之囚。

translations.literal: Zhao Chao was released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chao was released from prison.

sentences.zh: 北漢主收散卒，繕甲兵，完城塹以備周。

translations.literal: The ruler of Northern Han gathered scattered soldiers, repaired armor and weapons, and completed walls and moats to prepare against Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong gathered his scattered troops, repaired arms and armor, and strengthened walls and ditches against another Zhou advance.

sentences.zh: 楊兗將其眾北屯代州，北漢王遣王得中送兗，因求救於契丹，契丹主遣得中還報，許發兵救晉陽。

translations.literal: Yang Gun led his troops north to encamp at Daizhou. The king of Northern Han sent Wang Dezhong to escort Gun and, on that occasion, request aid from the Khitan. The Khitan ruler sent Dezhong back with a reply promising to dispatch troops to rescue Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun marched north to Daizhou. Liu Chong sent Wang Dezhong to escort him and, while doing so, plead for Khitan help. The Khitan ruler sent Dezhong back with a promise to march to the relief of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以符彥卿為河東行營都部署兼知太原行府事，以郭崇副之，向訓為都監，李重進為馬步都虞候，史彥超為先鋒都指揮使，將步騎二萬發潞州。

translations.literal: On renyin, Fu Yanqing was made Grand Commander of the Hedong Field Headquarters and concurrently Administrator of the Taiyuan Field Office, with Guo Chong as his deputy; Xiang Xun as overall supervisor; Li Chongjin as Chief Adjutant of Horse and Foot; Shi Yanchao as Vanguard Commander; and they led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry forth from Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Fu Yanqing was appointed grand commander of the Hedong field headquarters and acting administrator of the Taiyuan field office, with Guo Chong as his second, Xiang Xun as supervisor, Li Chongjin as chief adjutant of horse and foot, and Shi Yanchao as vanguard commander. They marched from Luzhou with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 仍詔王彥超、韓通自陰地關入，與彥卿合軍而進，又以劉詞為隨駕部署，保大節度使白重贊副之。

translations.literal: An edict further commanded Wang Yanchao and Han Tong to enter by Yindi Pass, unite their armies with Yanqing's, and advance together. Liu Ci was also made Escort Commander, with Bai Chongzan, Military Governor of Baoda, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Wang Yanchao and Han Tong to enter through Yindi Pass, join Fu Yanqing, and advance together, with Liu Ci as escort commander and Bai Chongzan, military governor of Baoda, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 漢昭聖皇太后李氏殂於西宮。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhao Sheng of Han, Lady Li, died in the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhao Sheng, Lady Li, died in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，北漢盂縣降。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Yuxian in Northern Han surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Yuxian in Northern Han surrendered.

sentences.zh: 符彥卿軍晉陽城下，王彥超攻汾州，北漢防禦使董希顏降。

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing's army reached beneath the walls of Jinyang. Wang Yanchao attacked Fenzhou, and Dong Xiyan, Defender of Northern Han, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing's army came up to Jinyang. Wang Yanchao invested Fenzhou, and Northern Han's defender Dong Xiyan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝遣萊州防禦使康延沼攻遼州，密州防禦使田瓊攻沁州，皆不下。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Kang Yanhao, Defender of Laizhou, to attack Liaozhou, and Tian Qiong, Defender of Mizhou, to attack Qinzhou, but neither city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Kang Yanhao, defender of Laizhou, against Liaozhou and Tian Qiong, defender of Mizhou, against Qinzhou, but neither city was taken.

sentences.zh: 供備庫副使太原李謙溥單騎說遼州刺史張漢超，漢超即降。

translations.literal: Li Qianpu of Taiyuan, Deputy Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse, went alone on horseback to persuade Zhang Hanchao, Prefect of Liaozhou, and Hanchao immediately surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianpu of Taiyuan, deputy commissioner of the supply depot, rode alone to Liaozhou and talked Zhang Hanchao into surrendering on the spot.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，葬聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝於嵩陵，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Sagely Divine, Respectful, Solemn, and Martial Cultural Emperor was buried at Songling, with the temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the late emperor was buried at Songling and given the temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 南漢主以高王弘邈為雄武節度使，鎮邕州。

translations.literal: The ruler of Southern Han appointed Prince Hongmiao of Gao as Military Governor of Xiongwu and stationed him at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han ruler made Prince Hongmiao of Gao military governor of Xiongwu and posted him to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘邈以齊、鎮二王相繼死於邕州，固辭，求宿衛，不許。

translations.literal: Hongmiao, because the Princes of Qi and Zhen had died in Yongzhou one after another, firmly declined and requested palace guard duty instead, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmiao refused firmly, pointing out that the princes of Qi and Zhen had both died at Yongzhou in succession, and asked instead for a post in the capital guard—but the court would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，委政僚佐，日飲酒，禱鬼神。

translations.literal: On reaching his post, he entrusted governance to his staff, drank wine daily, and prayed to spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: Once there he handed affairs to his staff, drank every day, and prayed to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 或上書誣弘邈謀作亂，戊午，南漢主遣甘泉宮使林延遇賜鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Someone submitted a memorial falsely accusing Hongmiao of plotting rebellion. On wuwu, the ruler of Southern Han sent Lin Yanyu, Commissioner of the Ganquan Palace, to bestow poisoned wine and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When someone memorialized falsely accusing Hongmiao of plotting rebellion, the Southern Han ruler sent Lin Yanyu of the Ganquan Palace on wuwu with poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 初，帝遣符彥卿等北征，但欲耀兵於晉陽城下，未議攻取。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor had dispatched Fu Yanqing and the others on the northern expedition, he had only wished to display military might beneath the walls of Jinyang and had not yet discussed taking the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first sent Fu Yanqing north, he meant only to show force beneath the walls of Jinyang, not to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 既入北漢境，其民爭以食物迎周師，泣訴劉氏賦役之重，願供軍須，助攻晉陽，北漢州縣繼有降者。

translations.literal: Once they had entered Northern Han territory, the people vied to welcome the Zhou army with food, weeping as they complained of the heavy taxes and corvée labor under the Liu house, expressing willingness to supply the army's needs and assist in attacking Jinyang. Northern Han prefectures and counties surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: But once inside Northern Han territory the people came out with food to welcome the Zhou armies, weeping over the Liu regime's crushing taxes and labor levies, offering supplies and begging them to take Jinyang. Prefecture after prefecture surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，始有兼併之意。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he first conceived the intention of annexation.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the Emperor began to think of annexing the state outright.

sentences.zh: 遣使往與諸將議之，諸將皆言「芻糧不足，請且班師以俟再舉。」

translations.literal: He dispatched messengers to go consult the generals. All the generals said, "Fodder and provisions are insufficient; we beg to withdraw the army for now and wait to launch again."
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to consult his commanders, who all replied that fodder and grain were running short and urged a temporary withdrawal until they could strike again.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 既而諸軍數十萬聚於太原城下，軍士不免剽掠，北漢民失望，稍稍保山谷自固。

translations.literal: Before long several hundred thousand troops gathered beneath the walls of Taiyuan. The soldiers could not avoid plundering. The people of Northern Han were disappointed and gradually took refuge in valleys and hills to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon hundreds of thousands of troops were massed before Taiyuan, and despite orders the soldiers could not help but loot. Northern Han's people lost heart and began hiding in the hills to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，馳詔禁止剽掠，安撫農民，止征今歲租稅，及募民入粟拜官有差，仍發澤、潞、晉、絳、慈、隰及山東近便諸州民運糧以饋軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he dispatched urgent edicts forbidding plunder, reassuring the farmers, halting collection of this year's rents and taxes, and recruiting civilians to contribute grain in exchange for offices of varying rank; furthermore he mobilized the people of Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and the convenient neighboring prefectures of Shandong to transport grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor responded with urgent orders against looting, reassured the peasants, canceled this year's taxes, and offered graded official appointments to anyone who contributed grain—while mobilizing the nearby prefectures to haul supplies to the front.

sentences.zh: 己未，遣李穀詣太原計度芻糧。

translations.literal: On jiwei, he dispatched Li Gu to Taiyuan to assess fodder and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he sent Li Gu to Taiyuan to survey the army's grain and fodder needs.

sentences.zh: 庚申，太師、中書令瀛文懿王馮道卒。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat Feng Dao, Prince Wenyi of Ying, died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Grand Preceptor and Chancellor Feng Dao, Prince Wenyi of Ying, died.

sentences.zh: 道少以孝謹知名，唐莊宗世始貴顯，自是累朝不離將、相、三公、三師之位，為人清儉寬弘，人莫測其喜慍，滑稽多智，浮沉取容，嘗著《長樂老敘》，自述累朝榮遇之狀，時人往往以德量推之。

translations.literal: Dao had been known from youth for filial piety and prudence. During Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang's reign he first rose to eminence, and from then on through successive dynasties he never departed from positions as general, chancellor, one of the Three Dukes, or one of the Three Preceptors. As a man he was pure and frugal, broad and magnanimous. No one could discern his pleasure or anger. He was witty and clever, floating and sinking as needed to win favor. He once wrote "Autobiography of a Long-lived Old Man," narrating in it the honors he had received through successive courts, and people of the time often praised him for virtue and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao had been renowned from youth for filial devotion and careful conduct. He rose to prominence under Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and thereafter never left high office—general, chancellor, one of the Three Dukes or Three Preceptors—through dynasty after dynasty. Pure and frugal, broad-minded and tolerant, he revealed neither pleasure nor anger; witty and shrewd, he rode each tide of fortune to keep his footing. His "Autobiography of the Long-lived Old Man" recounted his honors under one reign after another, and many contemporaries hailed him as a man of great moral stature.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修論曰：「禮義廉恥，國之四維。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu's commentary states: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame are the four cardinal bonds of a state.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu writes: "Propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame are the four pillars of a state.

sentences.zh: 四維不張，國乃滅亡。」

translations.literal: If the four cardinal bonds are not upheld, the state will perish."
translations.idiomatic: When these four fail, the state collapses."

sentences.zh: 禮義，治人之大法；

translations.literal: Ritual and righteousness are the great principles for governing people;
translations.idiomatic: Propriety and righteousness are the great principles by which people are governed;

sentences.zh: 廉恥，立人之大節。

translations.literal: integrity and shame are the great constants by which a person is established.
translations.idiomatic: integrity and shame are the great foundations of personal character.

sentences.zh: 況為大臣而無廉恥，天下其有不亂、國家其有不亡者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when one serves as a great minister yet lacks integrity and shame—could the realm fail to fall into chaos, or the state fail to perish!
translations.idiomatic: If even senior ministers lack integrity and shame, how can the realm stay stable or the state survive?

sentences.zh: 予讀馮道《長樂老敘》，見其自述以為榮，其可謂無廉恥者矣，則天下國家可從而知也。

translations.literal: When I read Feng Dao's "Autobiography of a Long-lived Old Man" and saw that he narrated these things as matters of honor, he can be called a man without integrity or shame; from this one can know what became of the realm and the state.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Feng Dao's autobiography, I find him boasting of his career as if it were glory itself—proof enough that he lacked all sense of shame, and from that one can read the fate of the age and the realm.

sentences.zh: 予於五代得全節之士三，死事之臣十有五，皆武夫戰卒，豈於儒者果無其人哉？

translations.literal: In my study of the Five Dynasties I found three men who preserved their integrity whole, and fifteen ministers who died for their cause—all of them warriors and soldiers. Can it truly be that among Confucian scholars there were none such?
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties I count only three men who kept their integrity intact and fifteen who died for their lord—all soldiers. Were there truly no such men among the literati?

sentences.zh: 得非高節之士，惡時之亂，薄其世而不肯出歟？

translations.literal: Could it be that men of lofty integrity, loathing the disorder of the times and disdaining the age, were unwilling to come forth?
translations.idiomatic: Were men of high principle simply sickened by the times and disdainful of the world, and therefore refused to serve?

sentences.zh: 抑君天下者不足顧，而莫能致之歟？

translations.literal: Or were those who ruled the realm unworthy of consideration, and thus unable to summon them forth?
translations.idiomatic: Or were the rulers themselves too contemptible to attract such men?

sentences.zh: 予嘗聞五代時有王凝者，家青、齊之間，為虢州司戶參軍，以疾卒於官。

translations.literal: I once heard that in the time of the Five Dynasties there was a man named Wang Ning, whose family lived between Qing and Qi. He served as Registrar of Households in Guo Prefecture and died of illness while in office.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard of one Wang Ning of the Five Dynasties, a native of the Qing-Qi region, who served as registrar in Guo Prefecture and died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 凝家素貧，一子尚幼，妻李氏，攜其子，負其遺骸以歸，東過開封，止於旅舍，主人不納。

translations.literal: Ning's family had always been poor. He had one son still young. His wife Lady Li, carrying their son and bearing his remains on her back, returned eastward. Passing through Kaifeng, she stopped at an inn, but the innkeeper would not receive her.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; their son was still small. Lady Li, his wife, set out eastward with the child and her husband's body on her back. In Kaifeng she sought lodging at an inn, but the keeper turned her away.

sentences.zh: 李氏顧天已暮，不肯去，主人牽其臂而出之。

translations.literal: Lady Li, seeing that night had come, refused to leave. The innkeeper dragged her by the arm and thrust her out.
translations.idiomatic: Night was falling and she would not go. The innkeeper seized her arm and dragged her out.

sentences.zh: 李氏仰天慟曰：「我為婦人，不能守節，而此手為人所執邪！」
